# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos_intel`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

```text
1	# MLflow channel for television (tv).
2	# Browse experiments, runs, and registered models against any MLflow tracking
3	# backend (file:./mlruns, sqlite:///path/to/mlflow.db, or http://server:port).
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   tv mlflow
7	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
8	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
9	#
10	# Prerequisites:
11	#   - `mlflow` installed (provided by dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools — the
12	#     CLI binary is what we exec under the `uv run --script` shebang of the
13	#     two helpers).
14	#   - `uv` on PATH (installed by uv role; required to resolve the PEP 723
15	#     inline-deps block in mlflow-source.py / mlflow-preview.py).
16	#
17	# Backend mode is resolved entirely from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI. When unset,
18	# mlflow 3.12+ auto-detects from $PWD: an `mlflow.db` file picks sqlite, an
19	# `mlruns/` dir picks file mode, otherwise it creates `mlruns/`. To pin a
20	# backend at launch time:
21	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://host:port tv mlflow
22	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
23	#
24	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
25	#   1. Experiments     all active experiments
26	#   2. Recent runs     top 50 runs across all experiments, by start_time desc
27	#   3. Runs (scoped)   runs in $MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID (hint row when unset;
28	#                      Alt+R on an experiment row sets it and re-launches tv)
29	#   4. Models          registered models from the model registry
30	#
31	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
32	#   1. Full JSON       params, metrics, tags, artifact_uri, timestamps
33	#   2. Metrics-only    sorted key=value table; or aggregated across recent
34	#                      runs for an experiment row
35	#
36	# Keybindings:
37	#   Enter      Context-aware:
38	#                experiment row -> re-launch tv scoped to that experiment's
39	#                                  runs (nested drill-in; Esc exits the
40	#                                  drilled view back to the shell)
41	#                run / model row -> open full JSON detail in pager
42	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard
43	#   Ctrl+O     Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only; prints a hint
44	#              otherwise)
45	#   Ctrl+B     Same as Ctrl+O — "B for browser" muscle-memory alias
46	#   Alt+R      Explicit drill — same as Enter on an experiment row,
47	#              available as a backup binding for muscle memory
48	#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal (paged)
49	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview
50	#   Ctrl+S     Cycle source
51	#
52	# No `watch` field: mlflow imports are heavy (~1s warm, several seconds cold);
53	# experiments and runs change on the minute scale anyway. Press Ctrl+R to
54	# refresh manually after logging a new run.
55	#
56	# Hint row sentinel: when the backend is unreachable or a source is unscoped,
57	# the helper emits a single row with id `__hint__`. Real mlflow ids never
58	# collide (experiment_ids are non-negative ints; run_ids are 32-hex; model
59	# names cannot contain `__hint__` in practice).
60	
61	[metadata]
62	name = "mlflow"
63	description = "MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models (file/sqlite/http backends)"
64	requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]
65	
66	[source]
67	command = [
68	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments",
69	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent",
70	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment",
71	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models",
72	]
73	display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  ({split:\\t:4})"
74	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
75	no_sort = true
76	
77	[preview]
78	# Helper always emits valid JSON now; pipe through `bat -l json` so the
79	# preview pane gets syntax highlighting (numbers, strings, keys). Same
80	# trick super-productivity.toml plays with `jq -C`, but bat's truecolor
81	# theme is easier on the eyes for nested objects.
82	#
83	# `--paging=never` is load-bearing: bat detects "not a TTY" inside TV's
84	# preview pipe and would otherwise still buffer; we want streamed output.
85	# `--plain` strips line numbers / decorations so the preview pane shows
86	# only the rendered content.
87	command = [
88	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full    | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
89	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view metrics | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
90	]
91	header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"
92	
93	[ui]
94	input_header = "MLflow"
95	
96	[ui.preview_panel]
97	size = 60
98	
99	[keybindings]
100	enter = "actions:open-or-drill"
101	# Override TV's default ctrl-y (which copies the entire display row) with
102	# id-only copy. Matches super-productivity.toml's convention.
103	ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
104	ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
105	# Ctrl+B is the muscle-memory alias — same action body as Ctrl+O. Reusing
106	# the existing action keeps the channel self-contained even if `mlf` (the
107	# umbrella CLI in dot_dotfiles/bin/) isn't installed.
108	ctrl-b = "actions:open-browser"
109	alt-r = "actions:drill-runs"
110	alt-j = "actions:dump-json"
111	
112	[actions.open-or-drill]
113	description = "Drill into experiment runs (experiment row) / open JSON detail (others)"
114	# Kind detection mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
115	#   __hint__       -> show the help JSON (helpful when MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is
116	#                     misconfigured: lets the user read the example URIs)
117	#   digit-only id  -> drill: re-exec tv with MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID + a
118	#                     --source-command override so the nested view shows ONLY
119	#                     this experiment's runs. Esc exits the drill back to
120	#                     the shell (TV does not have a back-stack; rerun
121	#                     `tv mlflow` for cross-experiment views).
122	#   anything else  -> open JSON detail in pager
123	#
124	# The header is set to "MLflow / <exp_name>" inside the drilled view so it's
125	# obvious you're in the nested context, not the top-level one. {split:\t:3}
126	# carries the experiment name in the experiments source layout (cols are:
127	# id, marker, lifecycle, name, last_update).
128	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
129	  __hint__) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
130	  *[!0-9]*) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
131	  *) MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" ;;
132	esac"""
133	mode = "execute"
134	
135	[actions.copy-id]
136	description = "Copy row id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard"
137	command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
138	mode = "fork"
139	
140	[actions.open-browser]
141	description = "Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only)"
142	# Build the URL inside the action so we read the live env var rather than
143	# baking it in. Inference mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
144	#   32-hex id -> need a roundtrip to find experiment_id, just open root
145	#   all-digit -> /#/experiments/<id>
146	#   else      -> /#/models/<name>
147	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; uri="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"; case "$uri" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) printf '[open-browser] needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://… — current: %s\\n' "${uri:-(unset)}"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$id" in __hint__) printf '[open-browser] no row selected\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; url="$uri/"; if [ "${#id}" = "32" ] && printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/0/runs/$id"; elif printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/$id"; else url="$uri/#/models/$id"; fi; if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url"; elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 & elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url"; else printf '[open-browser] no opener (open/xdg-open/wslview) — URL was: %s\\n' "$url"; sleep 2; fi"""
148	mode = "fork"
149	
150	[actions.drill-runs]
151	description = "Re-launch tv scoped to the highlighted experiment (Alt+R)"
152	# Same payload as the Enter drill branch — explicit binding for muscle
153	# memory and discoverability. No-op + hint on non-experiment rows so the
154	# user doesn't accidentally drill into an empty unscoped view.
155	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
156	  __hint__|*[!0-9]*) printf '[drill-runs] not an experiment row (id=%s). Move to the Experiments source (Ctrl+S) and try again.\\n' "$id"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;;
157	esac
158	MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" """
159	mode = "execute"
160	
161	[actions.dump-json]
162	description = "Print full JSON detail to terminal, paged"
163	command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
164	mode = "execute"
165

```text
1	# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
2	# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
3	# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
4	# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
5	# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
6	# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
7	#
8	# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
9	#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
10	#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
11	#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
12	# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
13	# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
14	#
15	# Usage:
16	#   tv fleet-hosts
17	#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
18	#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
19	#
20	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
21	#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
22	#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
23	#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
24	#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
25	#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
26	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
27	#
28	# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
29	# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
30	# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.
31	
32	[metadata]
33	name = "fleet-hosts"
34	description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
35	requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]
36	
37	[source]
38	command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
39	# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
40	# e.g.   lab-box <TAB> lab-box <TAB> alias:lab-box
41	#        vps-tokyo <TAB> 203.0.113.42 <TAB> explicit:dwlee@203.0.113.42
42	display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
43	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
44	
45	[preview]
46	command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"
47	
48	[keybindings]
49	enter = "actions:connect"
50	alt-t = "actions:probe"
51	alt-s = "actions:status"
52	alt-i = "actions:info"
53	alt-p = "actions:pueue"
54	
55	[actions.connect]
56	description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
57	command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
58	mode = "execute"
59	
60	[actions.probe]
61	description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
62	command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
63	mode = "execute"
64	
65	[actions.status]
66	description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
67	command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
68	mode = "execute"
69	
70	[actions.info]
71	description = "fleet info for this host"
72	command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
73	mode = "execute"
74	
75	[actions.pueue]
76	description = "fleet pueue for this host"
77	command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
78	mode = "execute"
79
```

<summary>Tool use: **Read**</summary>
 `./dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl`

```text
1	{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
2	# mac-apps channel — macOS GUI app control via Apple Events
3	#
4	# Pick a foreground GUI app, then choose a lifecycle action. Defaults are
5	# safe: Enter brings the app to front; destructive actions are Alt-gated.
6	#
7	# Pairs with: dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl (sourced by every action
8	#             to reuse appactivate / appquit / apprestart / appresponsive)
9	#             dot_config/television/cable/mac-procs.toml.tmpl (process picker,
10	#             sorted by compressed-aware memory — for profiling, not control)
11	#             dot_config/television/cable/kill-process.toml (cross-platform
12	#             process killer; default Enter = SIGTERM, no Apple Events)
13	#
14	# Why a separate channel from mac-procs / kill-process:
15	#   - kill-process Enter = SIGTERM — destructive for apps with state
16	#     (OrbStack VMs, Docker daemons, Slack drafts, unsaved buffers).
17	#   - mac-procs Enter = passthrough — for analysis, not lifecycle.
18	#   - mac-apps Enter = activate — non-destructive default; graceful Quit
19	#     is one Alt-key away and uses Apple Events so apps tear down cleanly.
20	#
21	# Usage:
22	#   tv mac-apps
23	#
24	# Keybindings:
25	#   Enter      Activate (bring to front)
26	#   Alt+Q      Graceful Quit (⌘Q-equivalent Apple Event) + reload
27	#   Alt+R      Quit + poll until gone + relaunch + reload
28	#   Alt+H      Hide app windows (System Events visible=false)
29	#   Alt+K      Force kill by PID (SIGKILL; last resort) + reload
30	#   Alt+I      Info pager: ps + full lsappinfo dump
31	#   Alt+P      Probe responsiveness (5s Apple Event timeout)
32	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (metadata <-> responsiveness)
33	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
34	#
35	# Why Alt+ rather than Ctrl+: tmux root-table `bind -n C-*` shadows inner
36	# apps. See CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule.
37	
38	[metadata]
39	name = "mac-apps"
40	description = "macOS apps — graceful quit / restart / activate / hide via Apple Events"
41	requirements = []
42	
43	[source]
44	# AppleScript exposes (unix id, name) for foreground GUI apps in one query.
45	# `background only is false` filters out daemons / agents / loginwindow etc.
46	# Output is "<pid>\t<name>\n" — matches `applist --pids` from the shell
47	# helper, but inlined so this channel works even before chezmoi-apply
48	# deploys the helper file.
49	command = """osascript -e 'tell application "System Events"' -e 'set out to ""' -e 'repeat with p in (every application process whose background only is false)' -e 'set out to out & (unix id of p) & tab & (name of p) & linefeed' -e 'end repeat' -e 'return out' -e 'end tell' 2>/dev/null"""
50	display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:1}"
51	# Default stdout when piping `tv mac-apps | ...` is the app NAME — what
52	# every helper (appquit/applaunch/appactivate/apprestart) wants on argv.
53	output = "{split:\\t:1}"
54	
55	[preview]
56	# Cycle 1: ps + lsappinfo. Fast (<50 ms).
57	# Cycle 2: responsiveness probe. ~2s per render — opt-in via Ctrl+F.
58	command = [
59	  """pid='{split:\\t:0}'

3	#
4	# Usage:

13	#   Ctrl+O     Toggle preview panel (TV global)

16	# Source format (TSV columns):
17	#   0. command    (raw; what gets printed / copied / executed)
18	#   1. label      (human-readable menu name matching VSCode/GitLens)
19	#   2. description
20	#   3. tag        ("⚠" for destructive, " " otherwise)
21	#   4. alias      (padded 10ch; oh-my-zsh git alias or *custom — searchable via fuzzy)

24	name = "git-ops"
25	description = "VSCode + GitLens Git operations: search, paste, copy, or exec"
26	requirements = ["awk", "git"]

28	[source]
29	command = """
30	awk -F'|' '/^[[:space:]]*\\|/ && $3 ~ /`/ {
31	  label=$2; cmd=$3; alias_=$4; desc=$5; notes=$6
32	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", label)
33	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", alias_)
34	  gsub(/`/, "", alias_)
35	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", desc)
36	  gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", notes)
37	  sub(/^[[:space:]]*`/, "", cmd); sub(/`[[:space:]]*$/, "", cmd)
38	  tag = (notes ~ /destructive/) ? "⚠" : " "
39	  aliaspad = sprintf("%-11s", alias_)
40	  printf "%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\t%s\\n", cmd, label, desc, tag, aliaspad
41	}' ~/.config/docs/tools/git-ops.md
42	"""

52	
53	[ui.preview_panel]

60	alt-e = "actions:exec"
61

[y/N]: '; read -r ans; case "$ans" in y|Y|yes|YES) eval "$cmd" ;; *) printf 'Aborted.\\n' ;; esac; printf '\\n[Press Enter to close]'; read -r _"""

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = [
5	#   "mlflow>=3.4",
6	#   "tyro>=0.9",
7	#   "rich>=13.9",
8	#   "plotext>=5.2",
9	#   "textual>=5.0",
10	# ]
11	# ///
12	"""mlf — umbrella CLI for MLflow operations.
13	
14	Bare `mlf` (no args) launches the interactive Textual TUI dashboard.
15	Subcommands below bypass it for scripted automation.
16	
17	Subcommands:
18	  tui                            Launch the interactive dashboard (default)
19	  tv [...]                       Launch `tv mlflow` (the fuzzy picker channel)
20	  open <id>                      Open the experiment / run / model page in browser
21	  copy <id>                      Copy an id to the clipboard
22	  plot <run_id> [metric...]      Terminal line plot of metric history (scripts/mlf/plot.py)
23	  list <kind> [...]              Tabular dump of experiments / runs / models (scripts/mlf/list.py)
24	  download <name>[@version|alias] Download a registered model's artifacts (scripts/mlf/download.py)
25	
26	Backend is read from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI (file:./mlruns | sqlite:///path | http(s)://host:port).
27	`open` requires an http(s):// URI; other subcommands work against all three.
28	
29	Mirrors the structure of `fleet` (see dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_fleet).
30	"""
31	from __future__ import annotations
32	
33	import os
34	import shutil
35	import subprocess
36	import sys
37	from pathlib import Path
38	
39	USAGE = """\
40	Usage: mlf [<subcommand>] [args...]
41	
42	Bare `mlf` (or `mlf tui`) launches the interactive Textual dashboard.
43	Subcommands bypass the TUI for scripted use.
44	
45	Subcommands:
46	  tui                                Launch the interactive dashboard
47	                                     (equivalent to bare `mlf`)
48	
49	  tv [args...]                       Open the `tv mlflow` fuzzy picker
50	                                     (passes argv + env through, including
51	                                      MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI / MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID)
52	
53	  open <id>                          Open in browser; auto-detects entity kind:
54	                                       32-hex  -> /#/experiments/<exp>/runs/<id>
55	                                       digits  -> /#/experiments/<id>
56	                                       else    -> /#/models/<name>
57	                                     Requires MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI to be http(s)://.
58	
59	  copy <id>                          Copy <id> to system clipboard
60	                                     (pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC52 fallback).
61	
62	  plot <run_id> [metric...]          Terminal plot of metric history. No metric
63	       [--width N] [--height N]      arguments = plot every key the run logged.
64	       [--theme NAME]
65	
66	  list experiments [--limit N]       Rich table or JSON dump.
67	  list runs [--experiment ID] [--limit N]
68	  list models [--limit N]
69	       [--json]                      Emit JSON to stdout for piping (jq-friendly).
70	
71	  download <name>[@<version|alias>]  Resolve via registry, then
72	           [--dest DIR]              mlflow.artifacts.download_artifacts().
73	                                     Default dest: ./<name>-<version>/.
74	
75	Examples:
76	  MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 mlf open 1
77	  mlf open cb250b888c5b41e98960b01360e4f41d
78	  mlf copy cb250b888c5b41e98960b01360e4f41d
79	  mlf plot cb250b888c5b41e98960b01360e4f41d loss accuracy
80	  mlf list runs --experiment 1 --limit 20
81	  mlf list models --json | jq '.[].id'
82	  mlf download MyModel@Champion --dest /tmp/champ
83	
84	See dot_config/television/cable/mlflow.toml for the tv-channel keybindings.
85	"""
86	
87	
88	def _source_path() -> Path:
89	    """Locate the chezmoi source dir. Required to import scripts.mlf.*.
90	
91	    Identical strategy to executable_fleet:_source_path. We trust `chezmoi
92	    source-path` when chezmoi is installed; otherwise fall back to the
93	    conventional ~/.local/share/chezmoi.
94	    """
95	    chezmoi = shutil.which("chezmoi")
96	    if chezmoi:
97	        try:
98	            out = subprocess.run(
99	                [chezmoi, "source-path"],
100	                capture_output=True, text=True, check=False, timeout=5,
101	            )
102	            if out.returncode == 0 and out.stdout.strip():
103	                return Path(out.stdout.strip())
104	        except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, OSError):
105	            pass
106	    fallback = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "chezmoi"
107	    if (fallback / "scripts" / "mlf" / "__init__.py").is_file():
108	        return fallback
109	    print(
110	        "mlf: cannot locate chezmoi source dir.\n"
111	        "  Tried: `chezmoi source-path` and ~/.local/share/chezmoi.\n"
112	        "  Install chezmoi or ensure the source dir exists.",
113	        file=sys.stderr,
114	    )
115	    sys.exit(2)
116	
117	
118	def _dispatch_tv(args: list[str]) -> int:
119	    """Exec `tv mlflow` with argv + env passthrough."""
120	    tv = shutil.which("tv")
121	    if not tv:
122	        print("mlf tv: `tv` (television) not in PATH", file=sys.stderr)
123	        return 2
124	    # Replace this process so signals (Ctrl+C) reach tv directly.
125	    os.execvp(tv, [tv, "mlflow", *args])
126	
127	
128	def _first_arg(args: list[str], sub: str) -> str | None:
129	    """Return args[0].strip() or None (with a friendly stderr message).
130	
131	    Centralised so both the CLI dispatchers and the TUI surface the same
132	    error format when an empty / missing id slips through.
133	    """
134	    if not args:
135	        print(f"mlf {sub}: missing <id> argument", file=sys.stderr)
136	        return None
137	    ident = args[0].strip()
138	    if not ident:
139	        print(f"mlf {sub}: empty <id>", file=sys.stderr)
140	        return None
141	    return ident
142	
143	
144	def _dispatch_open(args: list[str]) -> int:
145	    ident = _first_arg(args, "open")
146	    if ident is None:
147	        return 2
148	    from scripts.mlf import open_id
149	    return open_id(ident)
150	
151	
152	def _dispatch_copy(args: list[str]) -> int:
153	    ident = _first_arg(args, "copy")
154	    if ident is None:
155	        return 2
156	    from scripts.mlf import copy_id
157	    return copy_id(ident)
158	
159	
160	def _dispatch_plot(args: list[str]) -> int:
161	    sys.argv = ["mlf plot", *args]
162	    from scripts.mlf.plot import main as plot_main
163	    return plot_main()
164	
165	
166	def _dispatch_list(args: list[str]) -> int:
167	    sys.argv = ["mlf list", *args]
168	    from scripts.mlf.list import main as list_main
169	    return list_main()
170	
171	
172	def _dispatch_download(args: list[str]) -> int:
173	    sys.argv = ["mlf download", *args]
174	    from scripts.mlf.download import main as download_main
175	    return download_main()
176	
177	
178	def _dispatch_tui(args: list[str]) -> int:
179	    # Currently no flags; future opts (--theme, --restore-state) can parse `args`.
180	    _ = args
181	    from scripts.mlf.tui import main as tui_main
182	    return tui_main()
183	
184	
185	def main() -> int:
186	    # Help paths print USAGE and exit. `-h` / `--help` / `help` never enter
187	    # the TUI so `mlf -h | grep ...` and similar pipelines stay scriptable.
188	    if len(sys.argv) >= 2 and sys.argv[1] in ("-h", "--help", "help"):
189	        print(USAGE)
190	        return 0
191	
192	    src = _source_path()
193	    if str(src) not in sys.path:
194	        sys.path.insert(0, str(src))
195	
196	    # Bare `mlf` → TUI. Subcommands dispatch as usual.
197	    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
198	        return _dispatch_tui([])
199	
200	    sub = sys.argv[1]
201	    rest = sys.argv[2:]
202	
203	    dispatch = {
204	        "tui": _dispatch_tui,
205	        "tv": _dispatch_tv,
206	        "open": _dispatch_open,
207	        "copy": _dispatch_copy,
208	        "plot": _dispatch_plot,
209	        "list": _dispatch_list,
210	        "download": _dispatch_download,
211	    }
212	    fn = dispatch.get(sub)
213	    if fn is None:
214	        print(f"mlf: unknown subcommand '{sub}'\n\n{USAGE}", file=sys.stderr)
215	        return 2
216	    return fn(rest)
217	
218	
219	if __name__ == "__main__":
220	    sys.exit(main())
221
```

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Regenerate shell completion files for upstream CLIs.
3	#
4	# Usage:
5	#   scripts/generate_completions.sh [--force] [--quiet] [--help]
6	#
7	# Modes:
8	#   default   Skip tools whose completion file is already newer than the binary
9	#             (binary-mtime check — same idiom as 95_bitwarden.zsh / 47_mi_router.sh).
10	#   --force   Regenerate every tool's completion regardless of mtime.
11	#   --quiet   Suppress per-tool progress; still print final summary.
12	#
13	# Output paths (lazy-autoload conventions):
14	#   zsh:  ~/.zfunc/_<tool>                                              (in fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl:68)
15	#   bash: ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions/<tool>
16	#         (auto-loaded on first TAB by bash-completion v2)
17	#
18	# Tools NOT handled here (covered elsewhere — don't double-up):
19	#   sesh, tv, worktrunk        → shell-startup mtime check (dot_config/zsh/tools/{22_sesh,12_television,37_worktrunk}.zsh)
20	#   bw                         → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh)
21	#   marimo, thefuck, try-cli   → cached eval at startup    (dot_config/shell/{29_marimo,27_thefuck}.sh + dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh)
22	#   mi-router                  → tyro self-gen at startup  (dot_config/shell/47_mi_router.sh)
23	#   fleet, mlf, pqsum, x       → hand-written eager-load   (dot_config/{zsh/tools,bash}/45-49_*_completion.*)
24	#
25	# Invoked from:
26	#   - .chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_50_generate_completions.sh.tmpl   (every chezmoi apply, no --force)
27	#   - `just completions-refresh`                                          (manual, --force)
28	#
29	# Skip from chezmoi apply: export CHEZMOI_SKIP_COMPLETION_GEN=1
30	# Full design: docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md "How autocomplete works" + Section A.
31	
32	set -euo pipefail
33	
34	force=0
35	quiet=0
36	for a in "$@"; do
37	  case "$a" in
38	    --force) force=1 ;;
39	    --quiet) quiet=1 ;;
40	    -h | --help)
41	      sed -n '2,30p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \?//'
42	      exit 0
43	      ;;
44	    *)
45	      echo "generate_completions: unknown arg: $a" >&2
46	      exit 2
47	      ;;
48	  esac
49	done
50	
51	ZFUNC="${HOME}/.zfunc"
52	BASHDIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/bash-completion/completions"
53	
54	mkdir -p "$ZFUNC" "$BASHDIR"
55	
56	n_z_regen=0
57	n_b_regen=0
58	n_z_skip=0
59	n_b_skip=0
60	n_missing=0
61	
62	# regen <tool> <zsh-args> <bash-args>
63	# Uses word-splitting on $zargs / $bargs deliberately (the upstream completion
64	# subcommands are 1-3 words, no quoting needed).
65	regen() {
66	  local tool="$1" zargs="$2" bargs="$3"
67	  local bin
68	  if ! bin="$(command -v "$tool" 2>/dev/null)"; then
69	    n_missing=$((n_missing + 1))
70	    return 0
71	  fi
72	  local zfile="${ZFUNC}/_${tool}"
73	  local bfile="${BASHDIR}/${tool}"
74	
75	  # zsh
76	  if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -f "$zfile" ] || [ "$bin" -nt "$zfile" ]; then
77	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # word-split intentional
78	    if "$tool" $zargs >"$zfile.tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$zfile.tmp" ]; then
79	      mv "$zfile.tmp" "$zfile"
80	      n_z_regen=$((n_z_regen + 1))
81	      [ "$quiet" = 0 ] && printf '  zsh   %-10s → %s\n' "$tool" "$zfile"
82	    else
83	      rm -f "$zfile.tmp"
84	    fi
85	  else
86	    n_z_skip=$((n_z_skip + 1))
87	  fi
88	
89	  # bash
90	  if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -f "$bfile" ] || [ "$bin" -nt "$bfile" ]; then
91	    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
92	    if "$tool" $bargs >"$bfile.tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$bfile.tmp" ]; then
93	      mv "$bfile.tmp" "$bfile"
94	      n_b_regen=$((n_b_regen + 1))
95	      [ "$quiet" = 0 ] && printf '  bash  %-10s → %s\n' "$tool" "$bfile"
96	    else
97	      rm -f "$bfile.tmp"
98	    fi
99	  else
100	    n_b_skip=$((n_b_skip + 1))
101	  fi
102	
103	  # `set -e` + `[ test ] && cmd` at function tail is a bash footgun: when
104	  # `--quiet` makes the test fail, the &&-short-circuit returns 1, the inner
105	  # `if`-`then` body returns 1, regen() returns 1, and set -e aborts.
106	  return 0
107	}
108

127	regen pueue "completions zsh" "completions bash"

 `./dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_sesh-preview`

```text
1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# sesh-preview — multi-section preview for sesh fzf picker
3	#
4	# Sesh passes one argument that is either:
5	#   - an absolute path (zoxide / find sources)
6	#   - a session name like "icon  name  /path" (sesh's --icons output)
7	#
8	# We extract the path (last token), then render in this priority:
9	#   1. Header: dir name + git branch (if any) + last-modified
10	#   2. README.md (first 25 lines, syntax-highlighted via bat if available)
11	#   3. Recent git log (5 commits, oneline) — only if a git repo
12	#   4. Directory listing (eza tree if available, else ls)
13	#
14	# Designed to be safely called from sesh's preview_command. Stays under
15	# ~50 lines of output so fzf preview pane doesn't scroll on first paint.
16	
17	set -u
18	
19	raw="${1:-}"
20	[[ -z "$raw" ]] && exit 0
21	
22	# Extract the path: last whitespace-separated token. Works for both
23	# bare paths and sesh's "icon  name  /path" format.
24	path="${raw##* }"
25	# Strip trailing slash for consistency
26	path="${path%/}"
27	
28	# Sesh sometimes hands us the session name only (no path). Resolve via sesh.
29	if [[ ! -d "$path" ]]; then
30	    # Try interpreting whole arg as session name → ask sesh for its path
31	    resolved="$(sesh list -t -j 2>/dev/null | jq -r --arg n "$raw" \
32	        '.[] | select(.Name==$n) | .Path' 2>/dev/null | head -1)"
33	    [[ -n "$resolved" && -d "$resolved" ]] && path="$resolved"
34	fi
35	
36	[[ ! -d "$path" ]] && { echo "(not a directory: $path)"; exit 0; }
37	
38	# Color helpers — use tput if terminal supports it
39	if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
40	    bold=$(tput bold 2>/dev/null || true)
41	    dim=$(tput dim 2>/dev/null || true)
42	    reset=$(tput sgr0 2>/dev/null || true)
43	    cyan=$(tput setaf 6 2>/dev/null || true)
44	    yellow=$(tput setaf 3 2>/dev/null || true)
45	else
46	    bold="" dim="" reset="" cyan="" yellow=""
47	fi
48	
49	# ── 1. Header ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
50	name="$(basename "$path")"
51	parent_short="$(dirname "$path" | sed "s|^$HOME|~|")"
52	echo "${bold}${cyan}${name}${reset} ${dim}— ${parent_short}/${reset}"
53	
54	if git_branch=$(git -C "$path" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null); then
55	    git_status_count=$(git -C "$path" status --porcelain 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
56	    git_ahead_behind=$(git -C "$path" rev-list --left-right --count "@{upstream}...HEAD" 2>/dev/null \
57	        | awk '{ if ($1>0||$2>0) printf "↓%s ↑%s", $1, $2 }')
58	    echo "${dim}git:${reset} ${yellow}${git_branch}${reset} ${dim}(${git_status_count} dirty${git_ahead_behind:+, $git_ahead_behind})${reset}"
59	fi
60	
61	# Last modified (mtime of dir)
62	if mtime=$(stat -f "%Sm" -t "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M" "$path" 2>/dev/null); then
63	    echo "${dim}mtime: ${mtime}${reset}"
64	fi
65	
66	echo
67	
68	# ── 2. README ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
69	readme=""
70	for f in README.md README.rst README.txt readme.md README; do
71	    if [[ -f "$path/$f" ]]; then readme="$path/$f"; break; fi
72	done
73	
74	if [[ -n "$readme" ]]; then
75	    echo "${bold}── README ──${reset}"
76	    if command -v bat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
77	        bat --color=always --style=plain --line-range=:25 --paging=never "$readme"
78	    else
79	        head -25 "$readme"
80	    fi
81	    echo
82	fi
83	
84	# ── 3. Recent commits ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
85	if [[ -n "${git_branch:-}" ]]; then
86	    echo "${bold}── Recent commits ──${reset}"
87	    git -C "$path" log --oneline --color=always -5 2>/dev/null
88	    echo
89	fi
90	
91	# ── 4. Directory tree ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
92	echo "${bold}── Files ──${reset}"
93	if command -v eza >/dev/null 2>&1; then
94	    eza --tree --level=2 --git-ignore --color=always --icons \
95	        --ignore-glob='node_modules|.git|__pycache__|.venv|target|dist|build' \
96	        "$path" 2>/dev/null | head -30
97	else
98	    ls -la "$path" | head -25
99	fi
100

157	    """Copy `payload` to the clipboard. Returns exit code.
158	
159	    Provider chain: pbcopy → wl-copy → xclip → OSC 52 fallback to /dev/tty.
160	    Mirrors the shell snippet in mlflow.toml [actions.copy-id]. Pure helper
161	    so the TUI's `y` action can reuse it without spawning a subprocess.
162	    """
163	    providers = [
164	        ["pbcopy"],
165	        ["wl-copy"],
166	        ["xclip", "-selection", "clipboard"],
167	    ]
168	    for cmd in providers:

188	        with open("/dev/tty", "w") as tty:

204	def fetch_histories(
205	    client: "MlflowClient",
206	    run_id: str,
207	    keys: list[str],
208	) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[float]]], list[tuple[str, str]]]:
209	    """Fetch metric history for every key. Skip-on-error per key.
210	
211	    Returns (series, skipped) where:
212	      series  = {key: (steps_sorted, values_aligned), ...}
213	      skipped = [(key, "ExceptionType: message"), ...]
214	
215	    One slow / broken key (commonly a `system.*` metric over a flaky link)
216	    shouldn't abort the whole batch — both the CLI `mlf plot` and the TUI
217	    Plot tab surface skipped keys in a separate warning instead. Bump
218	    MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT for the whole invocation if a host needs
219	    longer per-key reads.
220	    """
221	    series: dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[float]]] = {}
222	    skipped: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
223	    for key in keys:
224	        try:
225	            history = client.get_metric_history(run_id, key)
226	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
227	            skipped.append((key, f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:80]}"))
228	            continue
229	        if not history:
230	            continue
231	        sorted_hist = sorted(history, key=lambda m: m.step)
232	        steps = [m.step for m in sorted_hist]
233	        values = [m.value for m in sorted_hist]
234	        series[key] = (steps, values)
235	    return series, skipped

27	The `fleet chezmoi <action>` namespace was introduced to free the top
28	level for generic primitives. `apply` / `status` / `diff` / etc. are NO
29	LONGER top-level subcommands — they only exist under `chezmoi`. The
30	`just fleet-*` recipes still call scripts/fleet/apply.py directly with
31	its underlying flags (`--readiness`, `--status`, `--kill-orphans`,
32	`--compact`, etc.) and continue to work unchanged.

52	                          Run chezmoi update --init across the fleet.
53	  chezmoi status          Pre-flight readiness probe (predicts apply outcome).
54	  chezmoi status --quick  Skip remote `git fetch` (faster).
55	  chezmoi status --live   Process-liveness probe (use during/after apply).

```text
1	# television (tv) Quick Reference
2	
3	[television](https://github.com/alexpasmantier/television) — blazing-fast TUI fuzzy finder with pluggable "channels".
4	
5	Custom channels: `dot_config/television/cable/` (chezmoi-managed)
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Basic Usage
10	
11	```bash
12	tv                   # Open interactive picker (default channel)
13	tv <channel>         # Open a specific channel, e.g. tv sesh
14	tv list-channels     # List all available channels
15	tv --help            # List all flags
16	```
17	
18	From tmux: `prefix + T` opens the sesh channel as a popup (see [Tmux Integration](#tmux-integration)).
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Community Channels
23	
24	tv has a built-in channel package manager. Run once after install (and periodically to update):
25	
26	```bash
27	tv update-channels
28	```
29	
30	This downloads [community-maintained channels](https://alexpasmantier.github.io/television/community/channels-unix) into `~/.config/television/cable/`. It:
31	
32	- **Skips** channels whose requirements aren't met on your system (e.g. `apt-packages` on macOS)
33	- **Skips** channels that already exist (won't overwrite custom channels)
34	- Covers git, docker, k8s, brew, cargo, GitHub, sesh, tmux, and many more
35	
36	Notable community channels: `sesh`, `git-branch`, `git-log`, `git-stash`, `git-diff`, `brew-packages`, `docker-containers`, `gh-issues`, `gh-prs`, `just-recipes`, `zoxide`, `zsh-history`, `env`, `dirs`, `files`, `text`.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## Custom Channels
41	
42	### `tools` channel
43	
44	Parses `~/.config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md` at runtime (deployed via chezmoi from `dot_config/docs/tools/`). The markdown file is the single source of truth — edit it to add or update tools.
45	
46	Open with `tv tools` or `prefix + U` in tmux.
47	
48	| Key | Action |
49	|-----|--------|
50	| `Enter` | Execute selected tool immediately |
51	| `Ctrl+/` | Toggle preview panel (tldr or `--help`) |
52	
53	For pasting an invocation to the shell buffer (with trailing space for tools that need arguments), use the fzf ZLE widget instead: **Alt+T** in any zsh session.
54	
55	---
56	
57	### `agent-wakeup` channel
58	
59	Dashboard for live coding-agent panes that are waiting on quota/rate-limit
60	resets. Open with `tv agent-wakeup` or tmux `prefix + M-a`.
61	
62	It shows each live agent pane, detected quota message, parsed reset time, and
63	any queued pueue wakeup task. `Alt+C` schedules `continue` at the detected
64	reset time plus a small buffer, `Alt+T` prompts for a custom time/delay,
65	`Alt+N` smart-sends immediately (`Enter` for Claude's `/rate-limit-options`
66	screen, otherwise `continue` + Enter), and `Alt+X` cancels queued wakeups.
67	
68	The shell wrapper is `agent-wakeup`; the shortcut
69	`agent-continue-at --pane %12 --at 01:52am` schedules a one-off wakeup
70	without opening TV. Full details: [Agent pane discovery](agent-panes-discovery.md#tv-agent-wakeup-quota-waits--scheduled-continue).
71	
72	---
73	
74	### `lan-devices` channel
75	
76	Fuzzy-search devices on the local subnet with open ports, MAC/vendor, hostname (rDNS + mDNS), ping RTT, and last-seen timestamp. Backed by `~/.config/television/lan-scan.sh`, which writes results incrementally to `~/.cache/tv/lan-devices.tsv` and per-host nmap detail to `~/.cache/tv/lan-ports/<ip>.txt`. The channel uses `watch = 2.0`, so rows stream into the picker as the background scan progresses (state column: `discovered` → `scanning` → `scanned`).
77	
78	Open with `tv lan-devices`, or run a synchronous scan first with the `lanscan` shell alias.
79	
80	**Sudo-gated with fallback:** when passwordless sudo is available (`sudo -n true`), the script uses `arp-scan -lgq` for the richest MAC/vendor data. Otherwise it falls back to `nmap -sn` ping sweep + OS ARP cache (`arp -an` on macOS, `ip neigh` on Linux). Vendor lookup for the fallback path uses nmap's `nmap-mac-prefixes` OUI database.
81	
82	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
83	
84	| Source | Description |
85	|--------|-------------|
86	| All devices | Every discovered host, sorted by IP (default) |
87	| With open ports | Only rows whose port count is ≥ 1 |
88	| Fresh only | Hosts seen within the last 5 minutes |
89	
90	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
91	
92	1. Cached nmap service detail (fast, from `~/.cache/tv/lan-ports/<ip>.txt`)
93	2. Live `nmap -sV -Pn -F` rescan (blocking, ~10–30 s)
94	3. ARP + rDNS + mDNS + ping metadata
95	
96	**Keybindings** (`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
97	
98	| Key | Action |
99	|-----|--------|
100	| `Enter` | Full `nmap -sV -A` in execute mode |
101	| `Alt+R` | Rescan ports on selected host + reload |
102	| `Alt+F` | Rescan full subnet (discover + ports) + reload |
103	| `Alt+D` | Re-discover only (no port scan) + reload |
104	| `Alt+S` | SSH to selected host |
105	| `Alt+H` | Open `http://<ip>` in the system browser |
106	| `Alt+C` | Clear scan cache + reload |
107	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy IP to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH) |
108	
109	**Cache layout:**
110	
111	```
112	~/.cache/tv/
113	├── lan-devices.tsv         # one row per device (watched by tv)
114	├── lan-ports/<ip>.txt      # nmap -sV output per host
115	├── lan-scan.log            # scan progress log
116	└── lan-scan.lock/          # mutex directory (removed on exit)
117	```
118	
119	Requires `nmap`; `rustscan` and `arp-scan` are used when present (all part of the `networking_tools` ansible role).
120	
121	---
122	
123	### `logs` channel
124	
125	Fuzzy-browse log files on the machine with colorful previews. Open with `tv logs`.
126	
127	Source file: [`dot_config/television/cable/logs.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/television/cable/logs.toml.tmpl) (chezmoi template — the journalctl cycle below is only rendered on Linux). Full toolbelt writeup: [log-tools.md](log-tools.md).
128	
129	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
130	
131	1. Project-local logs under `$PWD` — `.log` / `.ndjson` / `.jsonl` via `fd -HI`
132	2. User + system log dirs — `~/.cache/**/*.log`, `~/Library/Logs` on macOS, `/var/log/*.log` / `syslog*` / `messages*` (readable only)
133	3. **Linux only** — `journalctl --output=short-iso -n 2000` for systemd journal recent lines. Templated out on macOS because journalctl output lines are not file paths and the preview/Enter/Alt+T actions can't act on them (a dedicated `tv journalctl` channel would be the follow-up).
134	
135	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
136	
137	1. Colorful tail via [`tailspin`](https://github.com/bensadeh/tailspin) — `tail -n 500 FILE | tspin --print`; falls back to raw `tail` when `tspin` is missing
138	2. Plain [`bat`](https://github.com/sharkdp/bat) view — `bat --style=plain --color=always --line-range=:500` for unbiased comparison
139	
140	**Keybindings:**
141	
142	| Key | Action |
143	|-----|--------|
144	| `Enter` | Open in `lnav` (falls back to `ccze -A \| less -R`, then plain `less -R`) |
145	| `Alt+T` | Follow with `tspin --follow` (or `tail -F \| tspin --print` on older tailspin) |
146	| `Alt+E` | Open in `$EDITOR` |
147	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy file path to clipboard (OSC 52 over SSH) |
148	
149	Requires `fd` (part of the `base` ansible role). Tailspin, lnav, ccze are part of `devtools`.

153	### `services` channel
154	
155	Cross-platform fuzzy picker for systemd services (Linux) and launchd jobs (macOS), with tailspin-colored log previews and Alt-key lifecycle actions. Open with `tv services`.
156	
157	Source file: [`dot_config/television/cable/services.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/television/cable/services.toml.tmpl) (chezmoi template — Linux and macOS get different `systemctl` vs `launchctl` bodies). Full writeup including symbol legend and sudo caveats: [services.md](services.md).
158	
159	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
160	
161	1. Running only — active services, system + user merged
162	2. All loaded — active + inactive + failed among runtime-known units
163	3. Failed only — crashed / non-zero exit
164	4. User-scope only — `systemctl --user` / macOS `gui/$UID/` domain
165	5. **Installed on-disk** — every unit file / `.plist` on disk, with enablement badges (`✓ Enabled` / `○ Disabled` / `— Static` / `⊘ Masked` on Linux; `● Loaded` / `○ On-disk` on macOS). This is the "configured but not enabled" discovery view — land on a `○ Disabled` row, hit `Alt+L`, done.
166	
167	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
168	
169	1. Colorful log tail via tailspin — `journalctl -u NAME -n 500` on Linux; tails `StdoutPath` from `launchctl print` on macOS (prints a helpful message when no stdout is configured, rather than blocking on `log show`).
170	2. Status / details — `systemctl status` / `launchctl print`.
171	
172	**Keybindings:**
173	
174	| Key | Action |
175	|-----|--------|
176	| `Enter` | Follow live log (`journalctl -fu` / `tail -F StdoutPath \| tspin` or `log stream`) |
177	| `Alt+R` | Restart (auto-sudo when scope=system) |
178	| `Alt+S` | Stop (`systemctl stop` / `launchctl bootout`) |
179	| `Alt+T` | Start (`systemctl start` / `launchctl kickstart` with bootstrap-by-search fallback) |
180	| `Alt+U` | Reload (`reload-or-restart` / `launchctl kickstart`) |
181	| `Alt+D` | Show full status in pager |
182	| `Alt+E` | Edit unit file / plist in `$EDITOR` |
183	| `Alt+L` | Toggle enable-on-boot |
184	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy service name to clipboard |
185	
186	All mutating actions auto-prepend `sudo` when the row's scope column is `system`. Actions run in `execute` mode so the sudo password prompt is visible if needed.
187	
188	Deeper platform-specific channels (`tv systemd` with timers/sockets/targets + mask/daemon-reload; `tv launchd` with plist-on-disk sources + bootstrap/bootout) are planned follow-ups — see [`services.md`](services.md) for the full roadmap.
189	
190	No new dependencies — uses `systemctl`/`journalctl` (base systemd) on Linux, `launchctl`/`log` (macOS built-in) on Darwin, plus `tspin` from `devtools`.

193	
194	### `mac-procs` channel (macOS-only)
195	
196	Fuzzy-pick the heaviest macOS processes by **compressed-aware** memory (`top -l 1 -o mem`, matches Activity Monitor's "Memory" column). Open with `tv mac-procs`.
197	
198	Source file: [`dot_config/television/cable/mac-procs.toml.tmpl`](../../dot_config/television/cable/mac-procs.toml.tmpl) (chezmoi template gated on `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"`, so the channel only appears on macOS hosts).
199	
200	**Why this exists vs the generic `kill-process` channel**: `kill-process` sorts by RSS via `ps -axm`. On Apple Silicon, RSS does NOT include compressed or swapped pages — a process leaking 2 GB of compressed data shows as 100 MB in the RSS view. `mac-procs` uses `top -o mem` whose `mem` column is compressed-aware. See [macos-swap.md](macos-swap.md) for the full mental model.
201	
202	Source cycling (`Ctrl+S`):
203	
204	1. **Top by Memory** (compressed-aware, default) — matches Activity Monitor
205	2. **Top by CPU** — what's burning the fan / battery
206	3. **Top by virtual size** (`ps -axm` VSZ) — fragmented apps / Electron sniffing
207	
208	Preview cycling (`Ctrl+F`):
209	
210	1. `vmmap -summary <pid>` — VM region breakdown (no sudo)
211	2. `ps -p <pid> -o ...` — pid/ppid/user/etime/state/full command
212	3. `lsof -p <pid> | head -40` — top open files / sockets
213	
214	Keybindings: only `Enter` (passthrough) for now. Alt-key actions (kill, force-kill, footprint dump) are deliberately deferred — usage will be evaluated via the alias-only flow first; see the channel file header for candidate slots and the AGENTS.md "Keyboard shortcuts" matrix before claiming any new Alt slot.
215	
216	No new dependencies — `top`, `vmmap`, `ps`, `lsof` are all macOS built-ins.

223	
224	Open with `tv ansible`.
225	
226	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
227	
228	| Source | Description |

231	| Roles | Every role directory under `~/.ansible/roles/` |

237	2. Playbook → tag list within the file; role → directory listing; tag → roles referencing the tag

254	
255	### `git-ops` channel
256	
257	Fuzzy-search the full VSCode Source Control + GitLens command palette (~150 entries: pull/push, commit variants incl. amend, undo-last-commit, branch, rebase, cherry-pick, stash, tags, worktrees, submodule, config). Backed by `~/.config/docs/tools/git-ops.md` — the markdown table is the single source of truth; edit the table to change the channel.
258	
259	Each row also shows the matching **oh-my-zsh `git` plugin alias** (`gc!`, `gcam`, `gpf!`, `gst`, `grhh`, `gstp`, …) or repo-custom function (prefixed `*`, e.g. `*gcam-amend`, `*gundo`, `*lg`). That means you can fuzzy-search either by semantic name (`amend`, `undo`, `force push`), by the full `git …` invocation, **or** by the alias you half-remember — any of them lands on the same row.
260	
261	Open with `tv git-ops` (standalone) or press `Alt+I` in zsh to paste the selected command straight into the shell prompt.
262	
263	| Key | Action |
264	|-----|--------|
265	| `Enter` | Print selected command to stdout — captured by the `Alt+I` ZLE widget and inserted into `LBUFFER` |
266	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy command to clipboard (overrides TV default; pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC 52 fallback) |
267	| `Alt+E` | Confirm-prompt then `eval` the command (y/N); aborts by default on anything else |
268	| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview: matching row from `git-ops.md` ↔ `git help <subcommand>` |
269	| `Ctrl+O` | Toggle preview panel (TV global) |
270	
271	> `Alt+E` (not `Ctrl+E`) is used for execute so that TV's global `Ctrl+E = go_to_input_end` muscle memory is preserved inside the picker.
272	
273	Destructive rows (`commit --amend`, `reset --hard`, `push --force`, `branch -D`, `clean -fd`, `stash drop/clear`, `tag -d` on remote, rebase, etc.) are prefixed with `⚠` in the display line and trigger a red warning banner under `Alt+E`.
274	
275	Use-cases this solves:
276	
277	- "What's the exact `git commit --amend --no-edit` flag again?" — type `amend` or `gcn!`, Enter, done.
278	- "How do I undo the last commit without losing work?" — type `undo` or `gundo`, you see all three variants (soft / mixed / hard with the destructive tag).
279	- "Which alias force-pushes safely?" — type `force`, see `gpf` (with-lease, safe) next to `gpf!` (raw `--force`, destructive).
280	- Copy a command into a Cursor chat or a teammate's Slack without typing — `Ctrl+Y`.
281	- `git worktree`, `git submodule`, `git cherry-pick` — the commands nobody remembers the flags for.
282	
283	Adding a new command: append a row to the appropriate section of `dot_config/docs/tools/git-ops.md`:
284	
285	```markdown
286	| Menu Label | `git some-command --flag` | `gsf` | Short description | destructive |
287	```
288	
289	Columns are `Menu | Command | Alias | Description | Notes`. Leave the alias column blank (`| |`) if there's no oh-my-zsh alias; prefix with `*` if you're adding a custom function that lives in `dot_config/zsh/10_aliases.zsh`. See `docs/shells/aliases.md` for the full OMZ alias reference.
290	
291	Re-run `chezmoi apply` (md is deployed to `~/.config/docs/tools/`); no channel reload needed — it's parsed at runtime.
292

295	### `pueue` channel
296	
297	Interactive task manager for [pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) — fuzzy-search tasks, preview logs, and pause/resume/kill/restart without leaving the picker. Parses `pueue status --json` at runtime. Requires `pueue` and `jq`.
298	
299	Open with `tv pueue`. Auto-refreshes every 2 seconds.
300	
301	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
302	
303	| Source | Description |
304	|--------|-------------|
305	| All tasks | Every task, newest first (default) |
306	| Active only | Running + Queued + Paused tasks |
307	| Failed only | Tasks that exited non-zero |
308	| Groups overview | Pueue groups with status and parallelism |
309	
310	**Task management** (all `Alt+key` to avoid conflicts with TV built-ins and tmux):
311	
312	| Key | Action |
313	|-----|--------|
314	| `Enter` | Follow running task / view finished task log / show group status |
315	| `Alt+E` | Edit task command in `$EDITOR` (stashed/queued only) |
316	| `Alt+P` | Pause task |
317	| `Alt+R` | Resume/start task |
318	| `Alt+K` | Kill task |
319	| `Alt+T` | Restart task (in-place) |
320	| `Alt+X` | Remove task from list |
321	| `Alt+L` | Clean all finished tasks |
322	
323	**Clipboard:**
324	
325	| Key | Action |
326	|-----|--------|
327	| `Alt+Y` | Copy raw command to clipboard |
328	| `Alt+A` | Copy full `pueue add -w <path> -g <group> ...` command to clipboard |
329	
330	`Alt+Y` copies just the original command string. `Alt+A` reconstructs a full reproducible `pueue add` invocation including working directory, group, label, priority, and dependencies — useful for re-queuing or sharing tasks.
331	
332	**Group filtering:**
333	
334	| Key | Action |
335	|-----|--------|
336	| `Enter` | On groups view: show `pueue status -g <name>` text overview |
337	| `Alt+G` | Open a filtered view showing only the selected task's group |
338	
339	`Alt+G` extracts the group name from the selected entry and launches a new `tv` instance with `--source-command` filtered to that group. The filtered view has preview but not the full action keybindings. Quit to return to the main `tv pueue` channel. Enter on the groups source (cycle 4) shows a quick text overview via `pueue status -g`.
340	
341	**Preview** (`Ctrl+F` cycles):
342	
343	1. Task log output (`pueue log <id> --lines 200`) — piped through `tspin --print` when [tailspin](log-tools.md) is installed, for colored timestamps/levels/IPs/URLs. Falls back to raw output on fresh installs.
344	2. Full JSON task details (timing, dependencies, result — envs stripped for readability)
345	
346	**Implementation notes:**
347	
348	- All action keybindings use `Alt+` to avoid shadowing TV built-ins (`Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+K` for navigation, `Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+E` for input cursor, `Ctrl+R` for reload, etc.) and tmux root-table bindings (`C-h/j/k/l` for vim-tmux-navigator). Requires terminal to send Option as Meta (Ghostty: `macos-option-as-alt = left`).
349	- Uses jq's `@tsv` for output formatting — avoids TOML/shell escape conflicts with jq's `\(...)` interpolation syntax
350	- Clipboard actions are cross-platform: pbcopy (macOS), wl-copy (Wayland), xclip (X11), with OSC 52 fallback for remote SSH sessions (works through tmux with `set-clipboard on`)
351	- `Ctrl+Y` is overridden in the pueue channel to copy just the raw command (TV's default `ctrl-y` copies the full display line including ID, status, and group)
352	- `pueue edit` only works on stashed/queued tasks (pueue limitation); for running/finished tasks use `Alt+Y` to copy and re-add manually
353

355	
356	### `azure` channel
357	
358	Fuzzy-search Azure resources via `az` CLI with per-resource actions: restart / start / power-off / deallocate / rotate-public-IP / SSH / open-in-portal / delete / copy-id / switch-subscription. Backed by three helper scripts under `~/.config/television/` (`azure-source.sh`, `azure-preview.sh`, `azure-rotate-ip.sh`). Requires `az` (ansible `iac_tools` tag) and `jq`; the channel is automatically skipped on hosts without either.
359	
360	Open with `tv azure`. No auto-refresh — `az` calls are too slow to watch; hit `Ctrl+R` to reload.
361	
362	**Login gate:** if `az account show` fails, the channel shows a single synthetic row (`login · not-logged-in`). Press `Enter` to run `az login`, then `Ctrl+R` to reload.
363	
364	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
365	
366	| Source | Description |
367	|--------|-------------|
368	| Resource Groups | `az group list` (default) |
369	| Virtual Machines | `az vm list -d` — name, RG, location, power state |
370	| Public IPs | `az network public-ip list` — ipAddress + FQDN |
371	| NICs + NSGs | Union of `az network nic list` and `az network nsg list` |
372	| All resources | `az resource list` — generic fallback when you know a name but not its type |
373	
374	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
375	
376	1. `az <kind> show -o yaml` pretty-printed via `bat` when available
377	2. `az <kind> show -o json` for copy-paste / `jq` piping
378	
379	**Keybindings** (`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
380	
381	| Key | Action | Works on |
382	|-----|--------|----------|
383	| `Enter` | Show full resource (`az … show` in execute mode); on the login row runs `az login` | all |
384	| `Alt+R` | Restart VM | vm |
385	| `Alt+S` | Start VM | vm |
386	| `Alt+P` | Power-off VM (still billed) | vm |
387	| `Alt+D` | Deallocate VM (not billed) | vm |
388	| `Alt+I` | **Rotate public IP** — keeps the FQDN, swaps the IP | vm |
389	| `Alt+H` | SSH via `az ssh vm` (requires the `ssh` az extension) | vm |
390	| `Alt+O` | Open resource in Azure Portal (`open` / `xdg-open` / `wslview`) | all |
391	| `Alt+X` | Delete with y/N confirm | rg / vm / pip / nic / nsg / res |
392	| `Alt+U` | Switch subscription (fzf picker of `az account list`) | all |
393	| `Ctrl+Y` / `Alt+Y` | Copy resource id to clipboard (pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC 52 fallback) | all |
394	
395	Actions internally `case $kind` on the row's kind field, so wrong-kind keys (e.g. `Alt+R` on an RG row) print a 1-second "only applies to VMs" toast and no-op — same idiom as the `ansible` channel's role-only `Alt+V`.
396	
397	**Rotate Public IP** (`Alt+I`) calls `~/.config/television/azure-rotate-ip.sh <rg> <vm>`, a stateless port of [`DockerCompose-V2Ray/scripts/az_rotate_ip.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/DockerCompose-V2Ray/blob/main/scripts/az_rotate_ip.sh). It:
398	
399	- Resolves VM → NIC → PIP → DNS label live via `az` (no `.secrets/` state file).
400	- Refuses to run when `SSH_CONNECTION` is set (detaching the PIP would sever the SSH session before reattach).
401	- Requires Standard SKU (Basic retired 2025-09-30) with a `dnsSettings.domainNameLabel` — nothing to preserve otherwise.
402	- 5-step: detach → delete → recreate with same `--dns-name` → reattach → `dig +short <fqdn>` verify.
403	- `AZ_YES=1 azure-rotate-ip.sh <rg> <vm>` skips the confirm prompt (useful for scripting; the TV channel runs interactively so the prompt is fine).
404	
405	Use case: the GFW bans an Azure VM's public IP. Rotating keeps the `*.cloudapp.azure.com` FQDN, the TLS cert, the client configs, everything — the only change is the underlying IP.
406	
407	**Multi-subscription:** `Alt+U` pipes `az account list` through `fzf` so you can `az account set` without leaving the picker, then reloads the source. The `[ui].input_header` simply reads "Azure" — resolving the current subscription at channel-init time is cheap but not worth the UX complexity of refreshing it after `Alt+U`.
408	
409	**Non-goals (v1):** provisioning (`az vm create` stays in the V2Ray repo), teardown beyond `Alt+X`, and Windows-specific VM operations.
410

412	
413	### `clash` and `clash-api` channels
414	
415	Clash now ships as two TV channels:
416	
417	- `tv clash` — YAML-backed browsing of the resolved Clash profile.
418	- `tv clash-api` — live browsing of the external-controller API.
419	
420	Both channels reuse the same helpers under `~/.config/television/`:
421	
422	- `clash-parse.py` — PyYAML parser with `uv run --script` shebang.
423	- `clash-source.sh` — TSV source emitter for both YAML-backed and API-backed rows.
424	- `clash-preview.sh` — preview dispatcher for YAML, API, latency, and context views.
425	
426	Requires `curl` (base role). `uv` is required for YAML parsing and optional for pure env-driven API use. `bat` and `jq` are optional.
427	
428	#### `tv clash`
429	
430	Open with `tv clash`.
431	
432	**YAML discovery** (first match wins):
433	
434	1. `$CLASH_CONFIG` — explicit override, hard-fails if the path does not exist.
435	2. `~/.config/clash/profiles/list.yml` → active `profiles/<time>.yml`
436	3. `~/.config/clash/config.{yaml,yml}`
437	4. `~/.config/mihomo/config.{yaml,yml}`
438	5. `~/Library/Application Support/{clash,mihomo}/config.{yaml,yml}` (macOS)
439	
440	The important split is:
441	
442	- YAML rows (`proxies`, `proxy-groups`, `rules`, `summary`, `server`, `path`) come from the resolved profile, usually the active `profiles/<time>.yml`.
443	- Controller operations still prefer the runtime `external-controller` from the live Clash config, because profile files commonly keep stale controller ports like `127.0.0.1:9090` while the running app uses a different local port.
444	
445	Examples:
446	
447	```bash
448	tv clash
449	CLASH_CONFIG="$HOME/.config/clash/profiles/1731944239843.yml" tv clash
450	```
451	
452	If a resolved YAML has no `proxies[]`, `proxy-groups[]`, or `rules[]`, the channel emits a single informative `none` row instead of TV's generic "no stdout" placeholder. When no config exists at all, `Enter` on the `none` row still seeds `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` and opens `$EDITOR`.
453	
454	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
455	
456	| Source | Description |
457	|--------|-------------|
458	| Proxies | One row per `proxies[]` entry — `name`, `type`, `server:port`, compact `tls/udp/network/cipher` flags |
459	| Proxy Groups | One row per `proxy-groups[]` entry — `name`, `type`, current first member, `N members` |
460	| Rules | One row per `rules[]` entry, indexed `#NNNN` |
461	| Summary | Top-level YAML scalars plus `proxies.count` / `proxy-groups.count` / `rules.count` |
462	| API | Live controller health via `/version`, runtime `/configs`, and `/connections` counters |
463	
464	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
465	
466	1. Main — selected YAML block (API rows switch to controller JSON)
467	2. Latency — `/proxies/:name/delay` when the controller is reachable, else TCP + ping fallback
468	3. Meta — YAML context: groups referencing a proxy, group YAML, selected rule, or API detail
469	
470	#### `tv clash-api`
471	
472	Open with `tv clash-api`.
473	
474	Controller discovery:
475	
476	1. `$CLASH_CONTROLLER` / `$CLASH_SECRET`
477	2. Runtime `external-controller` from the local Clash config
478	3. Reachable Docker/local controller at `127.0.0.1:9090`
479	
480	Examples:
481	
482	```bash
483	tv clash-api
484	CLASH_CONTROLLER=192.168.222.207:9090 tv clash-api
485	CLASH_CONTROLLER=192.168.222.207:9090 CLASH_SECRET=mytoken tv clash-api
486	```
487	
488	`tv clash-api` does not add an in-UI host switch. Remote targeting stays env-driven on purpose.
489	
490	**Source cycling** (`Ctrl+S`):
491	
492	| Source | Description |
493	|--------|-------------|
494	| Proxies | Live `/proxies` leaf entries (rows without `all`) |
495	| Proxy Groups | Live `/proxies` selector-style entries (rows with `all`) |
496	| Rules | Live `/rules` entries |
497	| Summary | `/version`, `/configs`, `/connections` |
498	
499	**Preview cycling** (`Ctrl+F`):
500	
501	1. Main — controller JSON for the selected proxy, group, rule, or summary row
502	2. Latency — `/proxies/:name/delay` for proxies and `/proxies/:group` detail for groups
503	3. Meta — proxy-group references, group members/history, and nearby rules
504	
505	**Shared keybindings** (`Alt+` namespace avoids tmux/TV conflicts):
506	
507	| Key | Action | Applies to |
508	|-----|--------|------------|
509	| `Enter` | Show full detail for the selected row | both |
510	| `Alt+T` | Latency test | both |
511	| `Alt+S` | Switch a proxy-group's selection to the highlighted proxy | both |
512	| `Alt+C` | Close all connections (`DELETE /connections`) | both |
513	| `Alt+R` | Reload Clash config (`PUT /configs?force=true`) | both |
514	| `Alt+D` | Open `http://<host>/ui` or fall back to `yacd.haishan.me` | both |
515	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy `server:port` when YAML can resolve it, else copy the row name | both |
516	| `Alt+Y` | Copy the row name | both |
517	| `Alt+E` | Edit the resolved YAML config in `$EDITOR` | `clash` only |
518	
519	Notes:
520	
521	- All mutating actions (`Alt+S/C/R`) probe `/version` first; unreachable controllers no-op with a clear message.
522	- If no explicit env override is set, a stale or missing YAML `external-controller` falls back to `127.0.0.1:9090` when that API answers. This covers Docker Clash containers published as `0.0.0.0:9090->9090/tcp`.
523	- `tv clash-api` can reload a remote controller only when `CLASH_CONFIG` points at a config path that is meaningful on that controller host. If the remote host differs from the local runtime controller and no explicit `CLASH_CONFIG` is provided, `Alt+R` refuses with an explanation instead of sending a bad local path.
524	
525	**Redaction hardening**
526	
527	The sample configs users paste into `.specstory/history/`, `.cursor/plans/`, `.claude/plans/`, and `.opencode/plans/` often contain vmess UUIDs and Azure proxy hostnames. Three rules in [`.gitleaks.toml`](../../.gitleaks.toml) catch them with `secretGroup = 1`, so `scripts/redact_secrets.py` rewrites only the sensitive capture:
528	
529	- `clash-vmess-uuid` — `uuid: 41871a7c-…` → `uuid: 418...c56`
530	- `clash-vmess-share-link` — `vmess://<base64>` → `vme...XYZ`
531	- `azure-cloudapp-hostname` — `<vm>.<region>.cloudapp.azure.com` → truncated host only
532	
533	Raw IPv4 proxy servers are intentionally not redacted by default; they are too noisy against legitimate examples of public DNS and CDN endpoints.
534	
535	---
536	
537	### `sesh` channel (community)
538	
539	Provided by `tv update-channels`. Source cycling through session types and directory search, with connect/kill actions.
540	
541	**Source cycling** (use `Ctrl+S` to cycle):
542	
543	| Source | Description |
544	|--------|-------------|
545	| All sessions | `sesh list --icons` (default) |
546	| Tmux sessions | `sesh list -t --icons` |
547	| Configured sessions | `sesh list -c --icons` |
548	| Zoxide directories | `sesh list -z --icons` |
549	| File search | `fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash ~` |
550	
551	**Action keybindings:**
552	
553	| Key | Action |
554	|-----|--------|
555	| `Enter` | Connect to selected session |
556	| `Ctrl+D` | Kill selected tmux session + refresh list |
557	
558	**Preview:** `sesh preview` — right panel.
559	
560	---
561	
562	## Tmux Integration
563	
564	| Binding | Action |
565	|---------|--------|
566	| `prefix + T` | Open sesh channel as a television popup |
567	| `prefix + g` | Open sesh session picker via fzf (alternative) |
568	
569	> For the full tmux session management keybinding reference, see `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
570	
571	---
572	
573	## Keybinding Conflicts with tmux
574	
575	TV's default `ctrl-h/j/k/l` bindings conflict with tmux's `vim-tmux-navigator` root-table pane navigation (`C-h/j/k/l`). The managed config (`dot_config/television/config.toml`) resolves this:
576	
577	| Default | Action | Remapped to | Notes |
578	|---------|--------|-------------|-------|
579	| `ctrl-j` | select_next_entry | _(removed)_ | Use `down` or `ctrl-n` |
580	| `ctrl-k` | select_prev_entry | _(removed)_ | Use `up` or `ctrl-p` |
581	| `ctrl-h` | toggle_help | `alt-h` | Mnemonic, no conflicts |
582	| `ctrl-l` | toggle_layout | `alt-l` | Overridden in pueue channel (clean) |
583	
584	All other TV defaults (`ctrl-s`, `ctrl-f`, `ctrl-r`, `ctrl-y`, etc.) are kept since they don't conflict with tmux root-table bindings.
585	
586	---
587	
588	## Tips
589	
590	- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` — navigate results
591	- `Ctrl+P` / `Ctrl+N` — move up/down (vim users)
592	- `Alt+H` — toggle help panel (remapped from `ctrl-h` to avoid tmux conflict)
593	- Channels are defined as `.toml` files in `~/.config/television/cable/`
594	- Global config at `~/.config/television/config.toml` (chezmoi-managed from `dot_config/television/config.toml`)
595	- Run `tv update-channels` to get/update community channels
596	- Custom channels in this repo live at `dot_config/television/cable/` (deployed via chezmoi, won't be overwritten by `update-channels`)
597	- See [tv vs fzf](tv-vs-fzf.md) for comparison and channel best practices
598

Is it a TUI?

- The project states you can do "Everything you can do on GitHub - diff, comment, checkout, push, update etc." That explicitly lists diff, comment, checkout, push and update. It also integrates with the gh CLI and delta for diffs, and supports custom actions and keyboard hotkeys.

Configuration (config.yml / filters)
- Configuration is file-based: "Control every setting with a YAML config file."

Install command

What gh-select does
- It provides an interactive terminal UI to quickly find and inspect GitHub repos and only clone what you need.
- Key capabilities: fuzzy-search your repositories, browse a repo’s file tree without cloning, and perform partial (sparse) clones of selected folders.

Short quoted snippets (<=125 chars)
- "fuzzy-search your GitHub repositories"  
- "browse any repo's file tree without cloning"  
- "partial (sparse) clone only the folders you want"  
- "Zero extra dependencies — the TUI and GitHub API client are built in; no `fzf`, no `jq`."

Which repos are searched
- It filters the user's repositories (cached and refreshed in background) for instant fuzzy results.

Offered actions
- Clone repository (full)
- Browse & partial clone (open tree, mark folders, clone with sparse checkout)
- Copy repository name or URL
- Open repository in browser

Does it use fzf?
- No. The project explicitly says it does not require fzf or jq; the TUI and API client are built in.

Install & run
- As a gh extension: gh extension install remcostoeten/gh-select and run it as gh select
- Standalone: download a precompiled executable from Releases and run gh-select
- From source (Go): go install github.com/remcostoeten/gh-select@latest

Activity / maintenance
