<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://viktorsokolov.com/tips/interactively-clone-repositories-with-fzf`

```text
Below are the exact lines from the page that implement listing via gh, piping to fzf, the fzf flags shown, how the preview is generated, and how selected repos are cloned. Quoted lines are exact; other text paraphrases.

Exact gh + jq fetching line:
"repos=$(gh repo list --limit 1000 --json name,url,description,isArchived,isFork | \n  jq -r '.[] | select(.isArchived == false and .isFork == false) | \"\\(.url)\\t\\(.description // \"No description\")\"')"

Exact fzf invocation and flags:
"selected=$(echo \"$repos\" | \n  fzf --multi \n      --delimiter='\t' \n      --with-nth=1 \n      --preview 'echo {2}' \n      --preview-window=right:30%:wrap \n      --header=\"Select repos to clone (TAB to select multiple, ENTER to confirm)\" \n      --prompt=\"Repos > \" \n      --height=100% \n      --layout=reverse \n      --border)"

The preview generation (exact):
"--preview 'echo {2}'"
This prints the repository description column (the second field) into the preview pane.

Exact cloning loop that runs after selection (shows how clone-on-enter is performed):
"echo \"$selected\" | awk -F'\t' '{print $1}' | while read -r url; do\n  repo_name=$(basename \"$url\" .git)\n  if [ ! -d \"$repo_name\" ]; then\n    gh repo clone \"$url\"\n    echo \"✓ Successfully cloned $repo_name\"\n  fi\ndone"

Notes (paraphrased, not verbatim):
- The gh JSON invocation returns name,url,description,isArchived,isFork and jq filters out archived and forked repos and formats lines as "url<TAB>description".
- fzf is run with multi-select; Enter confirms the chosen lines and the script then extracts the URL field and clones each with gh repo clone.
- The page does not show any --bind mappings for extra actions, nor any wiring to "open in browser" — only the preview (description) and cloning behavior above are included.
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/gennaro-tedesco/gh-f`

```text
Quote: "the ultimate, compact and snappy `fzf` extension for `gh` cli."

Summary (paraphrased)
- gh-f is an fzf-based extension for the gh CLI that focuses on interactive in-repo workflows (PRs, branches, commits, tags, releases, logs, workflow runs, issue search and related git ops), not a general repo discovery/clone UI. Repository search/listing/cloning is handled by separate projects (see gh-s / gh-i).

Sub-features (from README)
- -p, prs: view, diff, checkout PRs (enter = checkout, ctrl-d = diff, ctrl-v = view)
- -b, branches: checkout, diff, delete branches (enter = checkout, ctrl-d = diff, ctrl-x = delete)
- -l, logs: view/diff/checkout commits (enter = checkout, ctrl-d = diff, ctrl-v = view patch)
- -t, tags: checkout/diff/view tags (enter = checkout detached HEAD, ctrl-d = diff, ctrl-v = view)
- -R, releases: checkout/diff release tags (same semantics as tags)
- -r, runs: show GitHub workflow runs and filter logs (enter = search run logs)
- -g, greps: grep in files in revision history (interactive regex prompt, select files, show pattern in history)
- -s, search: search issues in any repository (interactive prompt)
- -m, myissue: search issues you opened (interactive prompt)
- -k, pick: cherrypick files between branches (enter = checkout cherrypicked files)
- -a, adds: add files to staging area (enter = add; ctrl-d = diff selected file)
- -e, envs: show git config list (enter = print selected config variable)
- -h, -V: help and version

Dependencies
- Required: fzf; GNU coreutils
- Optional: bat (falls back to less if not present)

Install command
- gh extension install gennaro-tedesco/gh-f

(Note: repo-discovery/search/cloning is provided by related extensions like gh-s; gh-f targets interactive filtering and in-repo Git/GitHub tasks.)
```
</details></tool-use>

<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/benelan/gh-fzf`

```text
Summary — what gh-fzf is
- gh-fzf is “An fzf wrapper around the GitHub CLI.”
- It wraps GitHub CLI listing commands and shows a preview while you fuzzy-find items.

Does it support repo listing, preview, clone/open?
- Yes. The repo command provides previews and repo actions (clone, open in browser via keybinding).
- Quoted capabilities: “An fzf wrapper around the GitHub CLI.” and “Open the selected repo (see `gh repo edit --help`)” (see repo keybindings).

Key repo & global keybindings (selected)
- Global:
  - "ctrl-o": Open the selected item in the browser
  - "ctrl-y": Copy the selected item's URL to the clipboard
  - "ctrl-r": Reload the list and fetch changes from GitHub
  - "alt-P": Toggle the preview window layout
  - "alt-H": Toggle displaying the header (keybinding hints)
- repo-specific:
  - enter: Edit the selected repo's settings
  - alt-i: Run gh fzf issue on the selected repo (view issues)
  - alt-p: Run gh fzf pr on the selected repo (view PRs)
  - alt-r: Run gh fzf run on the selected repo (view runs)
  - alt-C: Clone the selected repo
  - alt-F: Fork the selected repo
  - alt-c / alt-o / alt-s / alt-f: filters for private/public/source/forked repos

Which gh list subcommands it wraps
- The extension provides fzf wrappers for these GitHub CLI list-like commands: issue(s), pr(s), run(s), workflow(s), release(s), label(s), milestone(s), repo(s), gist(s), plus a search command (issues/prs/repos/commits/code).

Install & basic usage
- Prereqs: install gh and fzf (example): brew install gh fzf
- Authenticate: gh auth login
- Install extension: gh extension install benelan/gh-fzf
- Basic usage: gh fzf <command> [flags] — all args after the command are passed to gh
- Upgrade / version helpers:
  - gh extension upgrade gh-fzf
  - gh fzf upgrade
  - gh fzf version

Concise examples
- List repos with filters: gh fzf repo --no-archived --visibility private --topic cli
- Open a repo in browser: select it and press ctrl-o

Notes
- The tool shows a preview pane and supports many command-specific keybindings to run gh subcommands on the selected item.
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# 41_github.sh - GitHub URL helpers (shared bash + zsh).
2	# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/41_github.zsh. The original relied on
3	# zsh-only constructs for the URL parsing:
4	#   ${(s:/:)url}      → split on `/`        — replaced with tr + while-read
5	#   ${(j:/:)slice}    → join with `/`       — replaced with an explicit loop
6	#   ${parts[N]}       → 1-indexed access    — replaced with an explicit loop
7	#   ${parts[5,-1]}    → slice               — replaced with an explicit loop
8	#   ${var:t}          → basename            — replaced with `${var##*/}`
9	#   ${#arr}           → array length        — replaced with `${#arr[@]}`
10	# setopt localoptions pipefail is gated on $ZSH_VERSION; bash falls back to
11	# `set -o pipefail` (leaks for the rest of the shell — benign).
12	
13	# Download a subdirectory from a GitHub repository tree URL.
14	# Example:
15	#   ghget https://github.com/microsoft/qlib/tree/high-freq-execution/examples/trade/
16	ghget() {
17	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
18	    emulate -L zsh
19	    setopt localoptions pipefail
20	  else
21	    # bash: no function-local options; setting pipefail leaks but is benign.
22	    set -o pipefail
23	  fi
24	
25	  local usage="Usage: ghget https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tree/<branch>/<path>"
26	  local branch_note="ghget currently supports only GitHub tree URLs with a single-segment branch name (no '/' in branch)."
27	
28	  if [ $# -ne 1 ]; then
29	    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
30	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
31	    return 1
32	  fi
33	
34	  local url="$1"
35	  local prefix="https://github.com/"
36	  if [[ "$url" != ${prefix}* ]]; then
37	    printf '%s\n' "Invalid GitHub tree URL: $url" >&2
38	    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
39	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
40	    return 1
41	  fi
42	
43	  url="${url#"$prefix"}"
44	  url="${url%%\?*}"
45	  url="${url%%\#*}"
46	  url="${url%/}"
47	
48	  # Portable split-on-/: `tr / \n | while read` (mirrors the svibe pattern
49	  # in dot_config/shell/22_sesh.sh — zsh disables word-splitting on
50	  # unquoted parameters by default, so the original `${(s:/:)url}` flag is
51	  # rewritten via tr + read).
52	  local -a parts
53	  parts=()
54	  local tok
55	  while IFS= read -r tok; do
56	    parts+=( "$tok" )
57	  done < <(printf '%s\n' "$url" | tr '/' '\n')
58	
59	  if [ "${#parts[@]}" -lt 5 ]; then
60	    printf '%s\n' "Invalid GitHub tree URL: $1" >&2
61	    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
62	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
63	    return 1
64	  fi
65	
66	  local owner repo tree_marker branch
67	  owner=""
68	  repo=""
69	  tree_marker=""
70	  branch=""
71	  local -a subdir_parts
72	  subdir_parts=()
73	  local idx=0
74	  for tok in "${parts[@]}"; do
75	    idx=$((idx + 1))
76	    case "$idx" in
77	      1) owner="$tok" ;;
78	      2) repo="$tok" ;;
79	      3) tree_marker="$tok" ;;
80	      4) branch="$tok" ;;
81	      *) subdir_parts+=( "$tok" ) ;;
82	    esac
83	  done
84	
85	  if [ "$tree_marker" != "tree" ]; then
86	    printf '%s\n' "Invalid GitHub tree URL: $1" >&2
87	    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
88	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
89	    return 1
90	  fi
91	
92	  # Subdir path = parts from index 4 onwards, joined with `/`.
93	  local subdir_path
94	  subdir_path=""
95	  for tok in "${subdir_parts[@]}"; do
96	    if [ -z "$subdir_path" ]; then
97	      subdir_path="$tok"
98	    else
99	      subdir_path="$subdir_path/$tok"
100	    fi
101	  done
102	
103	  # Leaf basename via parameter expansion (replaces zsh's `${var:t}` modifier).
104	  local leaf="${subdir_path##*/}"
105	
106	  if [ -z "$owner" ] || [ -z "$repo" ] || [ -z "$branch" ] || [ -z "$subdir_path" ] || [ -z "$leaf" ]; then
107	    printf '%s\n' "Invalid GitHub tree URL: $1" >&2
108	    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
109	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
110	    return 1
111	  fi
112	
113	  if [ -e "$leaf" ]; then
114	    printf '%s\n' "Destination already exists: $PWD/$leaf" >&2
115	    return 1
116	  fi
117	
118	  # Count path components (subdir depth) for `tar --strip-components=N`.
119	  local strip="${#subdir_parts[@]}"
120	
121	  local archive_root="${repo}-${branch}"
122	  local tmpdir
123	  tmpdir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ghget.XXXXXX")" || {
124	    printf '%s\n' "Failed to create temporary directory" >&2
125	    return 1
126	  }
127	
128	  printf '%s\n' "Downloading $owner/$repo/$subdir_path (branch: $branch) ..."
129	  if ! command curl -fsSL "https://github.com/$owner/$repo/archive/refs/heads/$branch.tar.gz" \
130	    | command tar -xz -C "$tmpdir" --strip-components="$strip" -f - "$archive_root/$subdir_path"; then
131	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
132	    printf '%s\n' "Failed to download or extract '$subdir_path' from '$owner/$repo' on branch '$branch'" >&2
133	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
134	    return 1
135	  fi
136	
137	  if [ ! -d "$tmpdir/$leaf" ]; then
138	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
139	    printf '%s\n' "Expected extracted directory was not found: $leaf" >&2
140	    return 1
141	  fi
142	
143	  if ! command mv -- "$tmpdir/$leaf" .; then
144	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
145	    printf '%s\n' "Failed to move extracted directory into: $PWD" >&2
146	    return 1
147	  fi
148	
149	  command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
150	}
```

```text
1	# 42_gitlab.sh - GitLab helpers using glab CLI (shared bash + zsh).
2	# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/42_gitlab.zsh; the only zsh-ism was
3	# `emulate -L zsh` (gated below).
4	
5	# ==============================================================================
6	# Method 1: Direct shell function (no AI agent needed)
7	# ==============================================================================
8	
9	# Create a GitLab repo under a group from the current git repo, set origin, and push.
10	# Detects current folder name as repo name and current branch automatically.
11	#
12	# Usage:
13	#   glcreate <group> [description]
14	#
15	# Examples:
16	#   glcreate david_quick_tries
17	#   glcreate david_quick_tries "My awesome project"
18	#
19	# If no description is given, the repo is created without one.
20	# The repo is created as private by default.
21	glcreate() {
22	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
23	
24	  local group="${1:?Usage: glcreate <group> [description]}"
25	  local desc="${2:-}"
26	  local name
27	  name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
28	  local branch
29	  branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
30	
31	  echo "Creating: ${group}/${name} (branch: ${branch})"
32	
33	  glab repo create "${group}/${name}" \
34	    --private \
35	    --defaultBranch "$branch" \
36	    --skipGitInit \
37	    ${desc:+--description "$desc"} \
38	  && {
39	    # Add or update origin remote
40	    git remote add origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git" 2>/dev/null \
41	      || git remote set-url origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git"
42	  } \
43	  && git push -u origin "$branch"
44	}
45	
46	# ==============================================================================
47	# Method 2: AI agent assisted (summarizes description from project content)
48	# ==============================================================================
49	
50	# Create a GitLab repo using an AI coding agent to inspect the project,
51	# auto-generate a description, create the repo, set origin, and push.
52	#
53	# Supported agents: opencode (default), claude, codex, cursor-agent
54	# Set GLCREATE_AGENT to change the default agent.
55	# Set GLCREATE_LANG to change the default prompt language (zh or en, default: zh).
56	#
57	# Usage:
58	#   glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent <name>] [--lang zh|en]
59	#
60	# Examples:
61	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries
62	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries "Override description"
63	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --agent claude
64	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --lang en
65	#
66	# If no description is given, the agent will summarize one from the project content.
67	glcreate-ai() {

69	
70	  local group="" desc="" agent="${GLCREATE_AGENT:-opencode}" lang="${GLCREATE_LANG:-zh}"

72	  # Parse arguments
73	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
74	    case "$1" in
75	      --agent) agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76	      --lang)  lang="$2"; shift 2 ;;
77	      *) [ -z "$group" ] && group="$1" || desc="$1"; shift ;;
78	    esac
79	  done
80	
81	  if [ -z "$group" ]; then
82	    echo "Usage: glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent opencode|claude|codex|cursor-agent] [--lang zh|en]"
83	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_AGENT env var to change default agent (default: opencode)"
84	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_LANG  env var to change default language (default: zh)"
85	    return 1
86	  fi
87	
88	  local name
89	  name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
90	  local branch
91	  branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
92	  local prompt
93	
94	  case "$lang" in
95	    en)
96	      prompt="Use glab to create a private repo under gitlab.com/${group}, repo name: ${name}, default branch: ${branch}. Set the origin remote and push.${desc:+ Description: ${desc}.} If no description is provided, summarize one sentence from the project content."
97	      ;;
98	    zh|*)
99	      prompt="用 glab 把這個 repo 建到 gitlab.com/${group} 底下，repo name: ${name}，private，default branch: ${branch}，設定 origin remote 並 push。${desc:+Description: ${desc}。}如果沒給 description 就根據項目內容總結一句。"
100	      ;;
101	  esac
102	
103	  echo "Agent: ${agent} | Lang: ${lang} | Repo: ${group}/${name} | Branch: ${branch}"
104	
105	  case "$agent" in
106	    opencode)       opencode run "$prompt" ;;
107	    claude)         claude -p "$prompt" ;;
108	    codex)          codex exec "$prompt" ;;
109	    cursor-agent)   cursor-agent -p "$prompt" ;;
110	    *)              echo "Unknown agent: ${agent}"; return 1 ;;
111	  esac
112	}
113
```

**Extensions (gh-dash, gh-notify)** — installed as `gh extension install owner/repo` in the same file, lines 1194-1234. The exact declarations:
```yaml
- name: Install gh-dash extension
  when: gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0 and (gh_extension_list.rc != 0 or 'dlvhdr/gh-dash' not in gh_extension_list.stdout)

# gh-notify (reuses the same probes):
```

**Idempotency** is handled by three `changed_when: false, failed_when: false` probe tasks that run once and are reused by both extensions (lines 1195-1219):
1. `command -v gh` → registers `gh_cli_path`
2. `gh auth status` → registers `gh_auth_status`

Each install is then gated on `gh_cli_path.rc == 0 and gh_auth_status.rc == 0 and (gh_extension_list.rc != 0 or '<owner>/<repo>' not in gh_extension_list.stdout)` — i.e. skipped if gh is absent, **skipped if gh is not authenticated** (so on a fresh unauthenticated box these are no-ops until a later `chezmoi apply`/ansible run after `gh auth login`), and skipped if the extension string already appears in `gh extension list`. # B) In-house CLI structure

## B5. Skeleton (shebang, subcommands, supporting-code layout)

Binaries live in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` (chezmoi's `executable_` prefix → deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/<name>` with +x; that dir is on PATH). Two flavors:

**Python-with-uv (mlf, pqsum, fleet, mi-router, reyee, ping-monitor)** — self-contained [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/) uv scripts. Shebang + inline metadata (from `executable_mlf`):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "mlflow>=3.4", "tyro>=0.9", "rich>=13.9", "plotext>=5.2", "textual>=5.0",
# ]
# ///
```
uv resolves the inline deps into a cached ephemeral env on first run — no venv management.

**Pure bash (x)** — `executable_x`: `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail`, subcommands via a `usage()` string and a `case "$cmd"` dispatcher (copy / copy-file / paste / open / help).

**Subcommand structure** — the Python umbrella CLIs (mlf, fleet) use a hand-rolled dispatcher, NOT argparse at the top level:
- A `USAGE` heredoc string; `main()` treats `sys.argv[1]` as the subcommand and looks it up in a `dispatch = {"tui": _dispatch_tui, "open": _dispatch_open, ...}` dict (`executable_mlf` lines 203-216).
- `-h`/`--help`/`help` short-circuit to print USAGE before any heavy import (so `mlf -h | grep` stays fast/scriptable); bare `mlf` launches the TUI.
- Each `_dispatch_*` lazily imports its implementation from the `scripts/<name>/` package and sets `sys.argv` for that submodule, e.g. `_dispatch_plot` does `sys.argv = ["mlf plot", *args]; from scripts.mlf.plot import main`.
- `pqsum` differs — it uses real `argparse` internally with a positional `mode` in `{text, ai, json}` plus many flags (`executable_pqsum` line 45, docstring lines 8-42).
- `fleet` adds a nested namespace (`fleet chezmoi <action>`) on the same dispatcher pattern (`executable_fleet` lines 47-89).

**Supporting code** lives in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/<name>/` as an importable package:
- `scripts/mlf/` → `__init__.py`, `plot.py`, `list.py`, `download.py`, `tui.py`
- `scripts/fleet/` → `__init__.py`, `apply.py`, `exec.py`, `hosts.py`, `info.py`, `pueue.py`, `tmux.py`

The bin script finds the repo at runtime and puts it on `sys.path` so `import scripts.mlf.*` works from any cwd — via `_source_path()` (`executable_mlf` lines 88-115), which runs `chezmoi source-path` and falls back to `~/.local/share/chezmoi`. mlf's docstring explicitly notes "Mirrors the structure of `fleet`."

## B6. Completion pattern (hand-written, two files per CLI, kept in sync)

Per `CLAUDE.md` row 23 + `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` Section F, a new in-house CLI needs **two hand-written files** ("Strategy B: eager-load," sourced at shell startup — distinct from Strategy A tyro self-gen used by mi-router, and NOT routed through `generate_completions.sh`):
- `dot_config/zsh/tools/<NN>_<name>_completion.zsh`
- `dot_config/bash/<NN>_<name>_completion.bash`

Numbering in use: 45 fleet, 46 mlf, 48 pqsum, 49 x, 50 ping-monitor, 51 dotcfg, 52 agent-warmup.

**zsh example** (`dot_config/zsh/tools/46_mlf_completion.zsh`) — guard, `_arguments -C` state machine, `_describe`, `compdef`:
```zsh
(( $+commands[mlf] )) || return 0
_mlf() {
    local context state state_descr line; typeset -A opt_args
    _arguments -C '1: :->subcommand' '*::arg:->args'
    case "$state" in
        subcommand)
            local -a subs=('tui:Launch...' 'tv:Launch tv mlflow...' 'open:...' 'plot:...' 'list:...' 'download:...')
            _describe -t subcommands 'mlf subcommand' subs ;;
        args) case "$line[1]" in list) _mlf_list ;; plot) _mlf_plot ;; ... esac ;;
    esac
}
compdef _mlf mlf
```

**bash twin** (`dot_config/bash/46_mlf_completion.bash`) — its header says "Mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/46_mlf_completion.zsh — keep both in sync":
```bash
command -v mlf >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
_mlf_completion() {
    local cur prev words cword; _init_completion -n = || return
    if [ "$cword" -eq 1 ]; then
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "tui tv open copy plot list download" -- "$cur") ); return
    fi
    # ... per-subcommand compgen -W / _filedir -d ...
}
complete -F _mlf_completion mlf
```

**Dynamic candidates shell out to the CLI itself** — e.g. `dot_config/zsh/tools/48_pqsum_completion.zsh` completes pueue group names via `pueue status --json | jq -r '.groups | keys[]'`; fleet host completion calls `fleet hosts --list`.

## B7. In-house CLIs ↔ tv-channel twins + the shared helper

Each Python umbrella CLI carries a `tv` subcommand that hands off to its Television channel. In `executable_mlf`, `_dispatch_tv` (lines 118-125) does:
```python
os.execvp(tv, [tv, "mlflow", *args])   # mlf tv  →  tv mlflow  (argv + env passthrough)
```
Channel definitions live in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/`: `mlflow.toml`, `pueue.toml`, `fleet-hosts.toml`, `git-ops.toml`.

**Shared helper: `scripts/mlf/__init__.py`** — the single source of truth imported by *all three* surfaces (the `executable_mlf` CLI shims, the `scripts/mlf/tui.py` dashboard, and mirrored into the tv preview script). It exports:
- `make_client()` — lazy `MlflowClient` (defers the ~1s `import mlflow` so `mlf -h`/`mlf tv` stay instant)
- `detect_kind(ident)` — classifies run/experiment/model; docstring notes it is "Kept in sync with `dot_config/television/executable_mlflow-preview.py:_detect_kind`"
- `open_id()`, `copy_id()` (clipboard chain pbcopy→wl-copy→xclip→OSC52), `fetch_histories()`, `tracking_uri()`, `ms_to_iso()`

Per `CLAUDE.md` row 21, the two UIs coexist by design (tv = fast fuzzy picker, mlf TUI = multi-pane dashboard) and deliberately **share single-letter mnemonics** — the TUI `BINDINGS` letters (`b`/`y`/`p`/`d`/`j`) equal the tv channel's `Ctrl+<letter>` actions in `mlflow.toml`; changing one requires changing the other in the same commit. Refactors go in `scripts/mlf/__init__.py`, not the call sites.

Extension **upgrades** are separate: handled by `cat_plugins` in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh` (`just upgrade-plugins`), per `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md:899`.

**To add a new gh extension**, the mechanism is: append a task block after line 1234 modeled on gh-notify (reuse the existing probes), then add the A-Z row in `docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md` (rows for existing extensions live at lines 305-306 and 999-1000).

# B) In-house CLI structure

## B5. Skeleton (shebang, subcommands, supporting-code layout)

Binaries live in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_*` (chezmoi's `executable_` prefix → deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin/&lt;name&gt;` with +x; that dir is on PATH). Two flavors:

**Python-with-uv (mlf, pqsum, fleet, mi-router, reyee, ping-monitor)** — self-contained [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/) uv scripts. Shebang + inline metadata (from `executable_mlf`):
```python
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --quiet --script
# /// script
# requires-python = "&gt;=3.11"
# dependencies = [
#   "mlflow&gt;=3.4", "tyro&gt;=0.9", "rich&gt;=13.9", "plotext&gt;=5.2", "textual&gt;=5.0",
# ]
# ///
```
uv resolves the inline deps into a cached ephemeral env on first run — no venv management.

**Pure bash (x)** — `executable_x`: `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail`, subcommands via a `usage()` string and a `case "$cmd"` dispatcher (copy / copy-file / paste / open / help).

**Subcommand structure** — the Python umbrella CLIs (mlf, fleet) use a hand-rolled dispatcher, NOT argparse at the top level:
- A `USAGE` heredoc string; `main()` treats `sys.argv[1]` as the subcommand and looks it up in a `dispatch = {"tui": _dispatch_tui, "open": _dispatch_open, ...}` dict (`executable_mlf` lines 203-216).
- `-h`/`--help`/`help` short-circuit to print USAGE before any heavy import (so `mlf -h | grep` stays fast/scriptable); bare `mlf` launches the TUI.
- Each `_dispatch_*` lazily imports its implementation from the `scripts/&lt;name&gt;/` package and sets `sys.argv` for that submodule, e.g. `_dispatch_plot` does `sys.argv = ["mlf plot", *args]; from scripts.mlf.plot import main`.
- `pqsum` differs — it uses real `argparse` internally with a positional `mode` in `{text, ai, json}` plus many flags (`executable_pqsum` line 45, docstring lines 8-42).
- `fleet` adds a nested namespace (`fleet chezmoi &lt;action&gt;`) on the same dispatcher pattern (`executable_fleet` lines 47-89).

**Supporting code** lives in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/scripts/&lt;name&gt;/` as an importable package:
- `scripts/mlf/` → `__init__.py`, `plot.py`, `list.py`, `download.py`, `tui.py`
- `scripts/fleet/` → `__init__.py`, `apply.py`, `exec.py`, `hosts.py`, `info.py`, `pueue.py`, `tmux.py`

The bin script finds the repo at runtime and puts it on `sys.path` so `import scripts.mlf.*` works from any cwd — via `_source_path()` (`executable_mlf` lines 88-115), which runs `chezmoi source-path` and falls back to `~/.local/share/chezmoi`. mlf's docstring explicitly notes "Mirrors the structure of `fleet`."

## B6. Completion pattern (hand-written, two files per CLI, kept in sync)

Per `CLAUDE.md` row 23 + `docs/zsh/zsh-completions.md` Section F, a new in-house CLI needs **two hand-written files** ("Strategy B: eager-load," sourced at shell startup — distinct from Strategy A tyro self-gen used by mi-router, and NOT routed through `generate_completions.sh`):
- `dot_config/zsh/tools/&lt;NN&gt;_&lt;name&gt;_completion.zsh`
- `dot_config/bash/&lt;NN&gt;_&lt;name&gt;_completion.bash`

Numbering in use: 45 fleet, 46 mlf, 48 pqsum, 49 x, 50 ping-monitor, 51 dotcfg, 52 agent-warmup.

**zsh example** (`dot_config/zsh/tools/46_mlf_completion.zsh`) — guard, `_arguments -C` state machine, `_describe`, `compdef`:
```zsh
(( $+commands[mlf] )) || return 0
_mlf() {
    local context state state_descr line; typeset -A opt_args
    _arguments -C '1: :-&gt;subcommand' '*::arg:-&gt;args'
    case "$state" in
        subcommand)
            local -a subs=('tui:Launch...' 'tv:Launch tv mlflow...' 'open:...' 'plot:...' 'list:...' 'download:...')
            _describe -t subcommands 'mlf subcommand' subs ;;
        args) case "$line[1]" in list) _mlf_list ;; plot) _mlf_plot ;; ... esac ;;
    esac
}
compdef _mlf mlf
```

**bash twin** (`dot_config/bash/46_mlf_completion.bash`) — its header says "Mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/46_mlf_completion.zsh — keep both in sync":
```bash
command -v mlf &gt;/dev/null 2&gt;&amp;1 || return 0
_mlf_completion() {
    local cur prev words cword; _init_completion -n = || return
    if [ "$cword" -eq 1 ]; then
        COMPREPLY=( $(compgen -W "tui tv open copy plot list download" -- "$cur") ); return
    fi
    # ... per-subcommand compgen -W / _filedir -d ...
}
complete -F _mlf_completion mlf
```

**Dynamic candidates shell out to the CLI itself** — e.g. `dot_config/zsh/tools/48_pqsum_completion.zsh` completes pueue group names via `pueue status --json | jq -r '.groups | keys[]'`; fleet host completion calls `fleet hosts --list`.

## B7. In-house CLIs ↔ tv-channel twins + the shared helper

Each Python umbrella CLI carries a `tv` subcommand that hands off to its Television channel. In `executable_mlf`, `_dispatch_tv` (lines 118-125) does:

Channel definitions live in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/`: `mlflow.toml`, `pueue.toml`, `fleet-hosts.toml`, `git-ops.toml`.

**Shared helper: `scripts/mlf/__init__.py`** — the single source of truth imported by *all three* surfaces (the `executable_mlf` CLI shims, the `scripts/mlf/tui.py` dashboard, and mirrored into the tv preview script). It exports:

Per `CLAUDE.md` row 21, the two UIs coexist by design (tv = fast fuzzy picker, mlf TUI = multi-pane dashboard) and deliberately **share single-letter mnemonics** — the TUI `BINDINGS` letters (`b`/`y`/`p`/`d`/`j`) equal the tv channel's `Ctrl+&lt;letter&gt;` actions in `mlflow.toml`; changing one requires changing the other in the same commit. Refactors go in `scripts/mlf/__init__.py`, not the call sites.

## 2. The concrete TOML schema (all field names)

Every channel is one TOML file. Tables and keys actually used across the 44 channels:

```
[metadata]
  name         = "channel-id"          # REQUIRED. what `tv <name>` matches; also the results in `tv list-channels`
  description  = "..."                  # shown in remote-control / channels list (supports multi-line """...""")
  requirements = ["gh", "jq"]           # binaries that must exist; channel is auto-SKIPPED if any missing

[source]
  command      = "shell cmd"            # OR an array (see below) → each array element is one "source" cycled with Ctrl+S
  command      = ["cmd1", "cmd2", ...]  # source cycling
  display      = "{split:\t:0}  ({split:\t:2})"   # how each row is rendered in the list (optional; default = whole line)
  output       = "{split:\t:0}"         # what is written to stdout on confirm_selection (for piping / shell integration)
  ansi         = true                   # source emits ANSI color; render it and strip for matching
  no_sort      = true                   # preserve source order (don't fuzzy-rank) — for pre-sorted sources
  watch        = 2.0                    # re-run source every N seconds (live refresh); omit for static

[preview]
  command      = "cmd using {…}"        # OR array → preview cycling with Ctrl+F
  command      = ["view1", "view2"]
  header       = "{split:\t:1}"         # text above the preview pane
  offset       = ...                    # (not used in this repo)

[ui]
  input_header = "MLflow"               # label in the input bar for this channel
  layout       = "portrait"             # per-channel orientation (global default is [ui].orientation="landscape")

[ui.preview_panel]                      # per-channel override of global preview panel
  size         = 60                     # percent width
  header       = "..."                  # (gh-issues uses inline form: preview_panel = { header = '...' })

[keybindings]
  enter  = "actions:open"               # bind a key → a custom action
  enter  = "confirm_selection"          # …or a built-in action
  alt-q  = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]   # …or an ARRAY = run custom action THEN a built-in

[actions.<name>]
  description = "Copy id to clipboard"  # shown in the action picker (Ctrl+X)
  command     = "shell cmd with {…}"    # placeholders substituted from the selected row
  mode        = "execute"               # or "fork" (see §4)
  shell       = "bash"                  # optional per-action shell override (git-repos.edit uses it)
```

Usage tallies confirm the surface: `command`×292, `description`×249, `mode`×206 (124 `execute` / 83 `fork`), `output`×34, `display`×24, `header`×30, `no_sort`×10, `watch`×6, `ansi`×7. Every channel has exactly `[metadata]`/`[source]`/`[preview]`/`[keybindings]`.

### The `{…}` placeholder mini-language (used in `display`, `output`, `preview.command`, `header`, and action `command`)
- `{}` — the entire selected line, raw (git-repos: `cd '{}'`)
- `{split:D:N}` — split line on delimiter `D`, take 0-indexed field `N`. `D` can be `\t`, a space, `/`, `#`, etc. Negative index allowed: `{split:/:-1}` = basename (last path segment).
- Ranges: `{split: :1..}` = fields 1→end.
- Pipes chain filters: `{strip_ansi|split: :1..|join: }` = strip ANSI, split on space, drop field 0, re-join with space. `strip_ansi` is required when `ansi = true` so actions receive clean text.

### Built-in actions (bindable in `[keybindings]`, defined in `config.toml`)
`quit`, `select_next_entry`/`select_prev_entry`, `select_next_history`/`select_prev_history`, `toggle_selection_down`/`_up`, `confirm_selection`, `scroll_preview_half_page_down`/`_up`, `cycle_previews` (Ctrl+F), `cycle_sources` (Ctrl+S), `copy_entry_to_clipboard` (Ctrl+Y — copies the whole display line), `reload_source` (Ctrl+R), `toggle_remote_control`, `toggle_action_picker` (Ctrl+X), `toggle_preview` (Ctrl+O), `toggle_help` (Alt+H), `toggle_layout` (Alt+L), `toggle_status_bar`, plus input-editing verbs.

## 3. Two representative channels, verbatim

### (a) `fleet-hosts.toml` — the house pattern: shell out to a CLI, TSV source, Alt-keyed side-effect actions
`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` (comments trimmed):

```toml
[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"          # emits:  name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]

[keybindings]

alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:pueue"

[actions.connect]

mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]

# … status / info / pueue actions follow the same shape …
```

### (b) `gh-prs.toml` — the community GitHub idiom: `gh … --json | jq`, `ansi=true`, `--web` open
`~/.config/television/cable/gh-prs.toml` (live, unmanaged — closest to your GitHub/GitLab repo channel):

```toml
[metadata]
name = "gh-prs"
description = "List GitHub PRs for the current repo"
requirements = ["gh", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''gh pr list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,createdAt,author,labels | jq -r 'sort_by(.createdAt) | reverse | .[] | "  \u001b[32m#\(.number)\u001b[39m   \(.title) \u001b[33m@\(.author.login)\u001b[39m" + (if (.labels | length) > 0 then " " + ([.labels[] | "\u001b[35m" + .name + "\u001b[39m"] | join(" ")) else "" end)'
'''
output = '{strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}'
ansi = true

[ui]
layout = "portrait"

[preview]
command = '''gh pr view '{strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}' --json number,title,body,state,... | jq -r ' ... '
'''

[actions.open]
description = "Open the PR in the browser"
command = "gh pr view {strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0} --web"
mode = "execute"

[actions.checkout]
description = "Checkout the PR branch locally"
command = "gh pr checkout {strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}"
mode = "execute"

[actions.merge]   # …and [actions.diff] …
command = "gh pr merge {strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}"
mode = "execute"
```

Note a real gotcha here: gh-prs/gh-issues define `[actions.open/checkout/merge/diff]` but have **no `[keybindings]` table**, so those actions are reachable only via the action picker (Ctrl+X). The chezmoi house style always binds keys explicitly. Also note `gh … --web` is how the community channels "open in browser" — simpler than the manual `open`/`xdg-open` chain (see §4).

The local-repo picker `~/.config/television/cable/git-repos.toml` is also worth reading verbatim — it shows `display = "{split:/:-1}"` (basename), `preview.command = "cd '{}'; git log … --graph --color"`, and actions `cd '{}' && $SHELL` / `${EDITOR:-vim} '{}'` with a per-action `shell = "bash"`.

---

## 4. How clone / open-in-browser / copy actions are wired

The mechanism is always: `[keybindings] <key> = "actions:<name>"` → `[actions.<name>]` with a `command` (placeholders filled from the selected row) and a `mode`.

**`mode` semantics (the load-bearing choice):**
- `mode = "fork"` — run detached, TUI stays open. Use for fire-and-forget: clipboard copy, browser open, kill/activate. (83 uses)
- `mode = "execute"` — suspend the TUI, run in the foreground terminal so the user sees output / can answer prompts / a pager. Use for ssh, `git log`, confirm-then-run, clone progress. (124 uses)
- Chaining a reload: `alt-q = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]` (mac-apps) runs the action then refreshes the list.

**Copy to clipboard (Ctrl+Y override).** TV's default `ctrl-y` copies the whole display line; channels override it to copy one field via an inline cross-platform `_clip()` helper. Canonical body from `git-ops.toml` `[actions.copy]` (identical in `mlflow.toml` `[actions.copy-id]`, mode `fork`):
```
_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return;
  if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy;
  elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy;
  elif command -v xclip  >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard;
  else printf '%b' "\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\007" > /dev/tty; fi; };   # OSC 52 for SSH
printf '%s' '{split:\t:0}' | _clip
```

**Open in browser (Ctrl+O in mlflow).** `mlflow.toml` `[actions.open-browser]` (mode `fork`) builds a URL then uses the opener fallback chain — this is the manual idiom to copy for a GitHub/GitLab web URL:
```
if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url";
elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url";
else printf '[open-browser] no opener — URL was: %s\n' "$url"; sleep 2; fi
```
The same `open`/`xdg-open`/`wslview` triad appears in `azure.toml` (Alt+O "open in portal") and `lan-devices` (Alt+H open `http://<ip>`). The simpler alternative for `gh` is just `gh repo view <owner/repo> --web` / `gh browse` (and `glab repo view --web`).

**Clone — does not exist yet in the repo.** No channel clones. Your closest structural precedents: `git-repos.toml` `[actions.cd]` (`cd '{}' && $SHELL`, execute) for "act on the selected repo path", and the `gh pr checkout` action (execute) for "run a `gh` subcommand on the selection." For a clone action you'd add e.g. `[actions.clone]` with `command = "gh repo clone {…} && …"` (or `git clone {…}`), `mode = "execute"` so clone progress is visible.

**Keybinding convention (important — from CLAUDE.md "Keybinding" cross-file rule, restated in every channel header).** tmux's root table binds `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), so custom side-effect actions use the **`Alt+<letter>`** namespace to avoid being shadowed: fleet-hosts, mac-apps, services, azure, pueue, ansible, lan-devices all use `Alt+`. `Ctrl+<letter>` is reserved for actions that mirror a TV global or override a benign default — `mlflow.toml` is the documented exception (`ctrl-y`=copy-id, `ctrl-o`=open-browser [overriding the global `toggle_preview`], `ctrl-b`=open-browser alias). `ctrl-y` overriding the default full-line copy is idiomatic and fine. If you add clone/open/copy, prefer `Alt+C`/`Alt+O`/`Ctrl+Y` and check the AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md "Keyboard shortcuts" matrix before claiming an Alt slot.

---

## 5. How channels are registered / discovered

**Auto-loaded — there is no registry.** tv loads every `*.toml` in `~/.config/television/cable/`; the `[metadata].name` becomes the channel id for `tv <name>` and `tv list-channels`. `config.toml` only holds global defaults (`default_channel = "files"`, global keybindings, UI, and `[shell_integration]` triggers that map shell commands → channels, e.g. `"git-repos" = ["nvim","code","hx","git clone"]`). Adding a channel = drop a `.toml` in the cable dir and `chezmoi apply`; no reload/registration step. `cable/channels.toml` is itself just a channel that `awk`-scans the cable dir's `[metadata]` blocks to list everything.

`tv update-channels` downloads community channels into the same dir but **skips files that already exist**, so your custom `.toml` files are never clobbered.

---

## 6. `.tmpl` templating & OS gating

Channel files may end `.toml.tmpl`; chezmoi renders the Go template and strips `.tmpl` on apply (`mac-apps.toml.tmpl` → `~/.config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml`). Two gating patterns are in use:

**Whole-file gate (channel exists only on matching OS/profile).** Wrap the entire file:
- `mac-apps.toml.tmpl` line 1: `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}` … line 128: `{{ end -}}`. On Linux the file renders empty → no channel.
- `mac-procs.toml.tmpl`: same `darwin` gate.
- `linux-apps.toml.tmpl` line 1: `{{- if and (eq .chezmoi.os "linux") (eq .profile "ubuntu_desktop") -}}` — gates on OS **and** profile.

**Inline per-OS bodies (one always-present channel, different source/action bodies).** `services.toml.tmpl` uses `{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "linux" }} … {{- else if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" }} … {{- end }}` around the systemctl-vs-launchctl source/preview/action commands. Same idiom in `disk.toml.tmpl`, `logs.toml.tmpl`, `sessions.toml.tmpl`, `scheduled-jobs.toml.tmpl`, `firewall.toml.tmpl`, `users.toml.tmpl`, `services-health.toml.tmpl`, `sysadmin.toml.tmpl`. Template data comes from `chezmoi data` (`.chezmoi.os`, `.profile`, etc.).

For your channel: if GitHub/GitLab picking is cross-platform, keep it plain `.toml` (no template). Use `.tmpl` only if a `source`/action body must differ by OS, or to hide the channel on hosts lacking `gh`/`glab` — though `requirements = ["gh"]` already auto-skips it when the binary is absent, which is the cleaner mechanism.

Also note the dormant-reference convention: `cable/sesh.toml.reference` deploys verbatim (chezmoi doesn't render/strip `.reference`), and because it isn't a `.toml`, tv ignores it — it's a kept-but-inactive override of the community `sesh` channel.

---

## 7. Preview commands & the `sesh-preview` helper

**How previews reference the selected line:** the `[preview].command` (or each element of the array form, cycled with Ctrl+F) uses the same `{…}` placeholders as actions. Examples:
- `fleet hosts --describe '{split:\t:0}'` (fleet-hosts)
- array cycling in `mlflow.toml`: `[…full JSON view…, …metrics view…]` each piped through `bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json`
- `git-repos.toml`: `cd '{}'; git log -n 200 --pretty=medium --all --graph --color`
- `sesh.toml.reference`: `sesh preview '{strip_ansi|split: :1..|join: }'`

**Preview helper script pattern.** Complex previews are extracted to a script rather than inlined. `sesh-preview` (`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_sesh-preview` → `~/.dotfiles/bin/sesh-preview`) is the model to copy for a repo preview: it takes the selected token as `$1`, resolves it to a directory, then renders a bounded (~50-line) multi-section view — header (dir + `git branch` + dirty/ahead-behind + mtime), README (first 25 lines via `bat`), recent `git log --oneline -5`, and an `eza --tree`/`ls` file listing, all with graceful fallbacks and `[[ -t 1 ]]` color gating. The mlflow/azure/clash channels follow the same split (`executable_<name>-source.{py,sh}` + `executable_<name>-preview.{py,sh}` under `dot_config/television/`, referenced as `~/.config/television/<name>-preview.py`). For a GitHub repo channel, a `github-preview` helper doing `gh repo view {owner/repo}` + README + recent commits would mirror this exactly.

---

## TL;DR for building your channel
Drop a plain `github-repos.toml` in `dot_config/television/cable/`. `[metadata]` with `requirements=["gh","jq"]` (auto-skips where absent). `[source].command` = `gh repo list … --json … | jq -r '…'` (or `glab`), with `ansi=true` + `output="{strip_ansi|…}"` if you colorize like gh-prs. `[preview]` = `gh repo view {…}` (optionally an array to cycle README ↔ commits, or a `github-preview` helper). Bind `enter`→clone/cd action (execute), `Alt+O`→`gh repo view {…} --web` (fork), `Ctrl+Y`→`_clip()` copy-URL (fork), `Alt+C`→`gh repo clone {…}` (execute). Crib structure from `fleet-hosts.toml` (house style) + `gh-prs.toml`/`git-repos.toml` (gh/repo idioms); crib the copy/open bodies from `mlflow.toml`/`git-ops.toml`.

There are 44 chezmoi-managed channel files in the cable dir; the live dir has 103 `.toml` (the rest are community channels from `tv update-channels`).

Key insight for your task: **there is NO chezmoi-managed `gh`/`glab` channel** (I verified — earlier `gh` grep hits were substring false positives like "high"/"through"). But `tv update-channels` has downloaded community reference channels that ARE on this machine and are the closest templates to what you want:

## 2. The concrete TOML schema (all field names)

Every channel is one TOML file. Tables and keys actually used across the 44 channels:

```
[metadata]
  name         = "channel-id"          # REQUIRED. what `tv &lt;name&gt;` matches; also the results in `tv list-channels`
  description  = "..."                  # shown in remote-control / channels list (supports multi-line """...""")
  requirements = ["gh", "jq"]           # binaries that must exist; channel is auto-SKIPPED if any missing

[source]
  command      = "shell cmd"            # OR an array (see below) → each array element is one "source" cycled with Ctrl+S
  command      = ["cmd1", "cmd2", ...]  # source cycling
  display      = "{split:\t:0}  ({split:\t:2})"   # how each row is rendered in the list (optional; default = whole line)
  output       = "{split:\t:0}"         # what is written to stdout on confirm_selection (for piping / shell integration)
  ansi         = true                   # source emits ANSI color; render it and strip for matching
  no_sort      = true                   # preserve source order (don't fuzzy-rank) — for pre-sorted sources
  watch        = 2.0                    # re-run source every N seconds (live refresh); omit for static

[preview]
  command      = "cmd using {…}"        # OR array → preview cycling with Ctrl+F
  command      = ["view1", "view2"]
  header       = "{split:\t:1}"         # text above the preview pane
  offset       = ...                    # (not used in this repo)

[ui]
  input_header = "MLflow"               # label in the input bar for this channel
  layout       = "portrait"             # per-channel orientation (global default is [ui].orientation="landscape")

[ui.preview_panel]                      # per-channel override of global preview panel
  size         = 60                     # percent width
  header       = "..."                  # (gh-issues uses inline form: preview_panel = { header = '...' })

[keybindings]
  enter  = "actions:open"               # bind a key → a custom action
  enter  = "confirm_selection"          # …or a built-in action
  alt-q  = ["actions:quit", "reload_source"]   # …or an ARRAY = run custom action THEN a built-in

[actions.&lt;name&gt;]
  description = "Copy id to clipboard"  # shown in the action picker (Ctrl+X)
  command     = "shell cmd with {…}"    # placeholders substituted from the selected row
  mode        = "execute"               # or "fork" (see §4)
  shell       = "bash"                  # optional per-action shell override (git-repos.edit uses it)
```

Usage tallies confirm the surface: `command`×292, `description`×249, `mode`×206 (124 `execute` / 83 `fork`), `output`×34, `display`×24, `header`×30, `no_sort`×10, `watch`×6, `ansi`×7. Every channel has exactly `[metadata]`/`[source]`/`[preview]`/`[keybindings]`.

### The `{…}` placeholder mini-language (used in `display`, `output`, `preview.command`, `header`, and action `command`)
- `{}` — the entire selected line, raw (git-repos: `cd '{}'`)
- `{split:D:N}` — split line on delimiter `D`, take 0-indexed field `N`. `D` can be `\t`, a space, `/`, `#`, etc. Negative index allowed: `{split:/:-1}` = basename (last path segment).
- Ranges: `{split: :1..}` = fields 1→end.
- Pipes chain filters: `{strip_ansi|split: :1..|join: }` = strip ANSI, split on space, drop field 0, re-join with space. `strip_ansi` is required when `ansi = true` so actions receive clean text.

### Built-in actions (bindable in `[keybindings]`, defined in `config.toml`)
`quit`, `select_next_entry`/`select_prev_entry`, `select_next_history`/`select_prev_history`, `toggle_selection_down`/`_up`, `confirm_selection`, `scroll_preview_half_page_down`/`_up`, `cycle_previews` (Ctrl+F), `cycle_sources` (Ctrl+S), `copy_entry_to_clipboard` (Ctrl+Y — copies the whole display line), `reload_source` (Ctrl+R), `toggle_remote_control`, `toggle_action_picker` (Ctrl+X), `toggle_preview` (Ctrl+O), `toggle_help` (Alt+H), `toggle_layout` (Alt+L), `toggle_status_bar`, plus input-editing verbs.

## 3. Two representative channels, verbatim

### (a) `fleet-hosts.toml` — the house pattern: shell out to a CLI, TSV source, Alt-keyed side-effect actions
`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` (comments trimmed):

```toml
[metadata]
name = "fleet-hosts"
description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]

[source]
command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"          # emits:  name&lt;TAB&gt;target&lt;TAB&gt;kind
display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[preview]
command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:connect"
alt-t = "actions:probe"
alt-s = "actions:status"
alt-i = "actions:info"
alt-p = "actions:pueue"

[actions.connect]
description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
mode = "execute"

[actions.probe]
description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
# … status / info / pueue actions follow the same shape …
```

### (b) `gh-prs.toml` — the community GitHub idiom: `gh … --json | jq`, `ansi=true`, `--web` open
`~/.config/television/cable/gh-prs.toml` (live, unmanaged — closest to your GitHub/GitLab repo channel):

```toml
[metadata]
name = "gh-prs"
description = "List GitHub PRs for the current repo"
requirements = ["gh", "jq"]

[source]
command = '''gh pr list --state open --limit 100 --json number,title,createdAt,author,labels | jq -r 'sort_by(.createdAt) | reverse | .[] | "  \u001b[32m#\(.number)\u001b[39m   \(.title) \u001b[33m@\(.author.login)\u001b[39m" + (if (.labels | length) &gt; 0 then " " + ([.labels[] | "\u001b[35m" + .name + "\u001b[39m"] | join(" ")) else "" end)'
'''
output = '{strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}'
ansi = true

[ui]
layout = "portrait"

[preview]
command = '''gh pr view '{strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}' --json number,title,body,state,... | jq -r ' ... '
'''

[actions.open]
description = "Open the PR in the browser"
command = "gh pr view {strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0} --web"
mode = "execute"

[actions.checkout]
description = "Checkout the PR branch locally"
command = "gh pr checkout {strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}"
mode = "execute"

[actions.merge]   # …and [actions.diff] …
command = "gh pr merge {strip_ansi|split:#:1|split:   :0}"
mode = "execute"
```

Note a real gotcha here: gh-prs/gh-issues define `[actions.open/checkout/merge/diff]` but have **no `[keybindings]` table**, so those actions are reachable only via the action picker (Ctrl+X). For your channel: if GitHub/GitLab picking is cross-platform, keep it plain `.toml` (no template). Use `.tmpl` only if a `source`/action body must differ by OS, or to hide the channel on hosts lacking `gh`/`glab` — though `requirements = ["gh"]` already auto-skips it when the binary is absent, which is the cleaner mechanism.

Also note the dormant-reference convention: `cable/sesh.toml.reference` deploys verbatim (chezmoi doesn't render/strip `.reference`), and because it isn't a `.toml`, tv ignores it — it's a kept-but-inactive override of the community `sesh` channel.

---

## 7. Preview commands &amp; the `sesh-preview` helper

**How previews reference the selected line:** the `[preview].command` (or each element of the array form, cycled with Ctrl+F) uses the same `{…}` placeholders as actions. Examples:
- `fleet hosts --describe '{split:\t:0}'` (fleet-hosts)
- array cycling in `mlflow.toml`: `[…full JSON view…, …metrics view…]` each piped through `bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json`
- `git-repos.toml`: `cd '{}'; git log -n 200 --pretty=medium --all --graph --color`
- `sesh.toml.reference`: `sesh preview '{strip_ansi|split: :1..|join: }'`

**Preview helper script pattern.** Complex previews are extracted to a script rather than inlined. `sesh-preview` (`/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_sesh-preview` → `~/.dotfiles/bin/sesh-preview`) is the model to copy for a repo preview: it takes the selected token as `$1`, resolves it to a directory, then renders a bounded (~50-line) multi-section view — header (dir + `git branch` + dirty/ahead-behind + mtime), README (first 25 lines via `bat`), recent `git log --oneline -5`, and an `eza --tree`/`ls` file listing, all with graceful fallbacks and `[[ -t 1 ]]` color gating. The mlflow/azure/clash channels follow the same split (`executable_&lt;name&gt;-source.{py,sh}` + `executable_&lt;name&gt;-preview.{py,sh}` under `dot_config/television/`, referenced as `~/.config/television/&lt;name&gt;-preview.py`). For a GitHub repo channel, a `github-preview` helper doing `gh repo view {owner/repo}` + README + recent commits would mirror this exactly.

---

## TL;DR for building your channel
Drop a plain `github-repos.toml` in `dot_config/television/cable/`. `[metadata]` with `requirements=["gh","jq"]` (auto-skips where absent). `[source].command` = `gh repo list … --json … | jq -r '…'` (or `glab`), with `ansi=true` + `output="{strip_ansi|…}"` if you colorize like gh-prs. `[preview]` = `gh repo view {…}` (optionally an array to cycle README ↔ commits, or a `github-preview` helper). Bind `enter`→clone/cd action (execute), `Alt+O`→`gh repo view {…} --web` (fork), `Ctrl+Y`→`_clip()` copy-URL (fork), `Alt+C`→`gh repo clone {…}` (execute). Crib structure from `fleet-hosts.toml` (house style) + `gh-prs.toml`/`git-repos.toml` (gh/repo idioms); crib the copy/open bodies from `mlflow.toml`/`git-ops.toml`.</result>

# Terminal repo browser/cloner (GitHub + GitLab) — research + build plan

Goal: replace hand-browsing `github.com/<user>?tab=repositories` and the limited
`gh repo list` with an interactive, fuzzy, Raycast-like terminal picker over repo
name+description with actions: **clone**, **open in browser**, **preview**. Same for
GitLab. Decide what to build vs install and how to package it in this chezmoi repo.

---

## 1. gh CLI capabilities (the raw materials)

Source: <https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_repo_list>

- `gh repo list [owner] --limit N` — **default limit is 30**; pass a big number to
  get everything: `gh repo list --limit 4000`. No documented hard cap.
- `--json <fields>` — full field set includes: `name`, `nameWithOwner`,
  `description`, `url`, `sshUrl`, `updatedAt`, `pushedAt`, `visibility`, `isFork`,
  `isArchived`, `isPrivate`, `isEmpty`, `primaryLanguage`, `languages`,
  `repositoryTopics`, `stargazerCount`, `forkCount`, `diskUsage`, `defaultBranchRef`,
  `homepageUrl`, `owner`, `parent`, `licenseInfo`, … (60+ fields).
- Filters: `--source` (non-forks only), `--fork` (forks only), `--archived`,
  `--no-archived`, `--visibility {public|private|internal}`, `--language`, `--topic`.
- Formatting: `--jq <expr>` (built-in jq) and `--template` (Go template).
- Actions: `gh repo clone <owner/repo> [dir]`, `gh repo view <owner/repo> --web`
  (open in browser), `gh browse -R <owner/repo>` (open; `-n/--no-browser` prints the
  URL instead — handy for copy). `gh repo view <owner/repo>` with no `--web` renders
  the **README** to the terminal (glamour markdown) → ideal fzf preview.
- `gh search repos <query>` (<https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_search_repos>) searches
  **all of GitHub** (`--owner`, `--limit` up to 1000, `--json`, `--sort`). Relevant
  only if you want repos you don't own or global topic search; for "my repos"
  `gh repo list` is the right primitive.

Canonical "all my repos as TSV of name+description":
\```bash
gh repo list "$owner" --limit 4000 --source --no-archived \
  --json nameWithOwner,description,sshUrl,updatedAt,visibility,primaryLanguage \
  --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // "")] | @tsv'
\```

## 2. Existing gh extensions for interactive/fuzzy repo finding

| Extension | URL | Repo browse+clone? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **gh-select** | <https://github.com/remcostoeten/gh-select> | **Yes — best fit** | Built-in Go TUI (no fzf/jq dep). Fuzzy-search *your* repos (cached), actions: full clone, browse file tree + sparse clone, **open in browser**, copy name/URL. `gh extension install remcostoeten/gh-select` → `gh select`. Active (v2.3.0, Jun 2026). GitHub-only. |
| **gh-fzf** | <https://github.com/benelan/gh-fzf> | Yes | fzf wrapper. `gh fzf repo [--no-archived --visibility private --topic cli]` with preview. Keys: `ctrl-o` open browser, `ctrl-y` copy URL, `ctrl-r` reload, `alt-C` clone, `alt-F` fork, `alt-c/o/s/f` filter private/public/source/fork. **Default `enter` = edit repo settings** (not clone). Wraps issue/pr/run/repo/gist/search. GitHub-only. |
| **gh-f** | <https://github.com/gennaro-tedesco/gh-f> | No | Compact fzf extension but **in-repo** workflows only (PRs, branches, logs, tags, issues). Repo discovery is its sibling `gh-s`. |
| **gh-repo-explore** | <https://github.com/samcoe/gh-repo-explore> | Partial | Interactively explore a repo's contents without cloning. Not a lister. |
| **gh-clone-org** | <https://github.com/abdianrizky/gh-clone-org> | Bulk | List org repos, fzf multi-select, parallel clone. Good for onboarding a whole org. |
| **gh-dash** | <https://github.com/dlvhdr/gh-dash> (<https://gh-dash.dev>) | **No** | Rich TUI **dashboard for PRs/issues** with per-repo config sections; actions diff/comment/checkout/push. Not a repo browser/cloner. **Already installed on this host** — keep it for PR/issue triage, it is the wrong tool for this task. |

## 3. fzf + gh canonical recipe

Simple community pattern (<https://viktorsokolov.com/tips/interactively-clone-repositories-with-fzf>):
\```bash
gh repo list --limit 1000 --json name,url,description,isArchived,isFork \
  | jq -r '.[] | select(.isArchived==false and .isFork==false)
            | "\(.url)\t\(.description // "No description")"' \
  | fzf --multi --delimiter='\t' --with-nth=1 \
        --preview 'echo {2}' --preview-window=right:30%:wrap
# then loop the selected URLs through `gh repo clone`
\```
Richer, recommended form (README preview via `gh repo view`; jain.rs shows GraphQL
variants: <https://jain.rs/devops/gh-fzf/>):
\```bash
sel=$(gh repo list "$owner" --limit 4000 --source --no-archived \
        --json nameWithOwner,description \
        --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // "")] | @tsv' \
      | fzf --ansi --delimiter='\t' --with-nth=1 \
          --preview 'gh repo view {1}' --preview-window='right,60%,wrap' \
          --bind 'ctrl-o:execute-silent(gh repo view {1} --web)' \
          --bind 'ctrl-y:execute-silent(gh browse -R {1} -n | pbcopy)' \
          --bind 'ctrl-r:reload(gh repo list "$owner" --limit 4000 ...)' \
          --header 'enter=clone+cd  ^o=open  ^y=copy-url  ^r=reload' \
      | cut -f1)
\```
Useful fzf tricks:
- `--preview 'gh repo view {1}'` renders the README in the pane (the killer feature).
- `--bind 'ctrl-o:execute-silent(gh repo view {1} --web)'` — open in browser without
  leaving the picker; `execute-silent` swallows output.
- `--bind 'ctrl-y:execute-silent(gh browse -R {1} -n | pbcopy)'` — copy URL.
- `enter:become(...)` (fzf ≥0.38) can replace fzf with the clone — **but** `become`
  runs in a child process and **cannot `cd` the parent shell**. To clone-then-cd,
  return the selection from fzf and run `clone && cd` in the enclosing shell function
  (see §6 — this is the decisive design constraint).

## 4. GitLab / glab

Sources: <https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/repo/list/>, <https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/repo/>

- `glab repo list` — **default per-page 30** (same trap as gh). Flags: `--all/-a`
  (every repo across pagination), `--per-page/-P`, `--page/-p`, `--group/-g`,
  `--include-subgroups/-G`, `--mine/-m`, `--member`, `--user/-u`, `--starred`,
  `--archived`, `--sort`, `--order`, `-F/--output json`, `--jq`.
- Get everything as JSON: `glab repo list --all --per-page 100 -F json`.
- JSON keys: `path_with_namespace`, `ssh_url_to_repo`, `http_url_to_repo`, `web_url`,
  `description`, `last_activity_at`, `visibility`.
- `glab repo clone <owner/project>`, `glab repo view <owner/project> --web` (`-w`);
  `glab repo view` also renders the README to the terminal for previews.
- Bulk clone idiom:
  `glab repo list --all -P 100 -F json | jq -r '.[].ssh_url_to_repo' | xargs -L1 git clone`
- **Self-hosted**: authenticate once `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.example.com`;
  then target it per-invocation with the `GITLAB_HOST` env var
  (`GITLAB_HOST=gitlab.example.com glab repo list …`) or set a default with
  `glab config set -h gitlab.example.com …`. (The list docs page doesn't restate
  this; it's standard glab host resolution.)
- No widely-adopted dedicated "glab-fzf" extension — the fzf pattern from §3 applied
  to `glab repo list -F json` is the pragmatic route, and keeps GitHub/GitLab
  symmetric.

## 5. Terminal Raycast-equivalents

- Closest to Raycast's "search repos → pick an action": **gh-select** (built-in TUI,
  fuzzy, clone/open/copy) and, in fzf form, **gh-fzf**.
- **gh-dash** is a PR/issue dashboard, not the repos analog — not a fit here.

## 6. Build vs install + packaging in THIS repo

### What a gh extension is
A repo whose root holds an executable named `gh-<name>` (a shell script with a
shebang, or a precompiled binary). `gh extension install <owner>/<repo>` symlinks it
onto PATH; `gh` auto-discovers it and runs it as `gh <name>`. Local dev:
`gh extension create <name>` scaffolds, `gh extension install .` links the cwd.
Precompiled (Go, etc.) via `gh extension create --precompiled=go` + release binaries.
Docs: <https://docs.github.com/en/github-cli/github-cli/creating-github-cli-extensions>,
<https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_extension>. Idiomatic **if you want to publish/share**.

### Local grounding (facts from this repo)
- `gh`, `glab`, and `gh-dash` are **already installed** (ansible devtools role
  `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`, tool list line 3 + tasks).
- Natural homes already exist: `dot_config/shell/41_github.sh` (has `ghget`) and
  `dot_config/shell/42_gitlab.sh` (has `glcreate`, `glcreate-ai`). Both are
  bash+zsh-shared.
- tv channel template: `dot_config/television/cable/git-ops.toml` — parses a doc as
  single source of truth, has `display`/`output`/`[preview]`/`[keybindings]` with
  `ctrl-y = actions:copy` and `alt-e = actions:exec` (fork/execute modes). ~40 custom
  channels exist; discoverable via `tv list-channels`.
- Clone-dir convention: repos live at **`/Volumes/Data/Program/<group>/<repo>`**
  (sesh wildcard `dot_config/sesh/sesh.toml` triggers a tmuxp project layout on
  `sesh connect`), plus `~/repos/*`. So the ideal clone action is:
  clone into `/Volumes/Data/Program/<owner>/<repo>` → `cd` (or `sesh connect`).
- Custom CLIs are `executable_<name>` in `dot_dotfiles/bin/` (on PATH).
- Existing docs: `docs/tools/gh-cli.md`; `gh` catalogued in
  `dot_config/docs/tools/cli-tools.md`.

### The decisive constraint
The workflow is **find → clone → start working in the repo**. Only code running in
the interactive shell (a **shell function** or ZLE widget) can `cd` the parent shell
into the freshly-cloned dir. A `gh` extension or a `tv` action runs in a subprocess
and **cannot change the caller's cwd** — it can clone but leaves you where you were.
Browse/open/copy have no such limit and work from any packaging.

### Recommendation (hybrid, in priority order)

1. **Primary — standalone shell functions `ghrepo` + `glrepo`** in the existing
   `dot_config/shell/41_github.sh` / `42_gitlab.sh`. Uses the §3 fzf-preview pattern:
   - preview = `gh repo view {1}` / `glab repo view {1}` (README);
   - `enter` → capture selection, `clone` into `/Volumes/Data/Program/<owner>/<repo>`,
     then `cd` there (optionally `sesh connect` to get the tmuxp layout);
   - `ctrl-o` → open in browser; `ctrl-y` → copy URL;
   - `glrepo` honors `GITLAB_HOST` for self-hosted; `--group/--mine` passthrough.
   Covers **both hosts symmetrically**, gets **clone+cd**, reuses the repo's own
   conventions, zero new dependencies, sits beside `ghget`/`glcreate`.

2. **Optional — mirror `tv` channels** `github-repos.toml` + `gitlab-repos.toml`
   (clone `git-ops.toml`). Great discoverable browse/open/copy surface + ZLE Alt-key
   widget; `enter` prints the `gh repo clone …` command (no auto-cd — the fork/execute
   limitation). Good complement, not a clone-workflow replacement.

3. **Optional zero-effort trial — `gh extension install remcostoeten/gh-select`**
   for a Raycast-like GitHub TUI out of the box (and add to the devtools tool list if
   kept). GitHub-only, no cd-after-clone, adds a Go binary — so it *complements* the
   function rather than replacing it.

- **Skip gh-dash** for this purpose (keep it for PR/issue triage).
- **gh-fzf** is a fine reference / drop-in if you'd rather not maintain fzf glue, but
  it's GitHub-only and its default `enter` edits settings — you'd rebind.
- If sharing/publishing ever matters, factor the picker into a `gh-repo` extension and
  keep a 3-line shell wrapper that adds the `cd`. More surface to maintain; only worth
  it for shareability.

### Cross-file maintenance (CLAUDE.md invariants — do in the same commit)
- New shell function → update `docs/shells/aliases.md` (+ any completion catalog).
- New `tv` channel → update `docs/tools/tv.md`, the `chezmoi-dotfiles` skill's channel
  list, and register/preview wiring as git-ops does.
- Installing gh-select → add to `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` tool list
  + `docs/tools/` note.
Read `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` Hard invariants + cross-file table first.

```bash
gh repo list --limit 1000 --json name,url,description,isArchived,isFork \
  | jq -r '.[] | select(.isArchived==false and .isFork==false) | "\(.url)\t\(.description // "No description")"' \
  | fzf --multi --delimiter='\t' --with-nth=1 --preview 'echo {2}' --preview-window=right:30%:wrap
# then loop selected URLs through `gh repo clone`
```
Richer form (README preview; GraphQL variants at https://jain.rs/devops/gh-fzf/):
```bash
sel=$(gh repo list "$owner" --limit 4000 --source --no-archived \
        --json nameWithOwner,description \
        --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // "")] | @tsv' \
      | fzf --ansi --delimiter='\t' --with-nth=1 \
          --preview 'gh repo view {1}' --preview-window='right,60%,wrap' \
          --bind 'ctrl-o:execute-silent(gh repo view {1} --web)' \
          --bind 'ctrl-y:execute-silent(gh browse -R {1} -n | pbcopy)' \
          --header 'enter=clone+cd  ^o=open  ^y=copy-url' \
      | cut -f1)
```
Key tricks: `--preview 'gh repo view {1}'` renders the README (killer feature); `execute-silent` for open/copy without leaving fzf; `gh browse -R {} -n` prints the URL. **Caveat:** `enter:become(...)` (fzf ≥0.38) runs in a child and **cannot `cd` the parent shell** — to clone-then-cd you must return the selection and run `clone && cd` in the enclosing shell function.

## 4. GitLab / glab
Sources: https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/repo/list/ , https://docs.gitlab.com/cli/repo/
- `glab repo list` — **default per-page 30** (same trap). Flags: `--all/-a` (all across pagination), `--per-page/-P`, `--page/-p`, `--group/-g`, `--include-subgroups/-G`, `--mine/-m`, `--member`, `--user/-u`, `--starred`, `--archived`, `--sort`, `--order`, `-F/--output json`, `--jq`.
- All-as-JSON: `glab repo list --all --per-page 100 -F json`. Keys: `path_with_namespace`, `ssh_url_to_repo`, `http_url_to_repo`, `web_url`, `description`, `last_activity_at`, `visibility`.
- `glab repo clone <owner/project>`, `glab repo view <owner/project> --web` (`-w`); `glab repo view` also renders the README for previews.
- Bulk: `glab repo list --all -P 100 -F json | jq -r '.[].ssh_url_to_repo' | xargs -L1 git clone`.
- **Self-hosted:** `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.example.com` once, then target per-call with the `GITLAB_HOST` env var (`GITLAB_HOST=gitlab.example.com glab repo list …`) or a default via `glab config set -h …`.
- No widely-adopted "glab-fzf" extension — apply the §3 fzf pattern to `glab repo list -F json` (keeps GitHub/GitLab symmetric).

## 5. Terminal Raycast-equivalents
Closest to "search repos → pick action": **gh-select** (built-in TUI) and, in fzf form, **gh-fzf**. **gh-dash** is a PR/issue dashboard, not the repos analog.

## 6. Build vs install + packaging
**What a gh extension is:** a repo whose root holds an executable named `gh-<name>` (shebang script or precompiled binary); `gh extension install <owner>/<repo>` puts it on PATH and `gh` runs it as `gh <name>`. Local dev: `gh extension create <name>` + `gh extension install .`. Idiomatic **if you want to share/publish**. Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/github-cli/github-cli/creating-github-cli-extensions , https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_extension

**Decisive constraint:** the workflow is find → clone → *work in the repo*. Only code in the interactive shell (a **shell function** / ZLE widget) can `cd` the parent into the freshly-cloned dir. A gh extension or a tv action runs in a subprocess and **cannot change the caller's cwd** — it clones but leaves you put. Browse/open/copy have no such limit.

### Recommendation (hybrid, priority order)
1. **Primary — standalone shell functions `ghrepo` + `glrepo`** added to the existing `41_github.sh` / `42_gitlab.sh`, using the §3 pattern: preview `gh/glab repo view {1}`; `enter` clones into `/Volumes/Data/Program/<owner>/<repo>` then `cd`s (optionally `sesh connect` for the tmuxp layout); `ctrl-o` open, `ctrl-y` copy URL; `glrepo` honors `GITLAB_HOST` + `--group/--mine`. Covers **both hosts**, gets **clone+cd**, reuses repo conventions, zero new deps, sits beside `ghget`/`glcreate`.
2. **Optional — mirror `tv` channels** `github-repos.toml` + `gitlab-repos.toml` cloned from `git-ops.toml` for a discoverable browse/open/copy surface + ZLE Alt-key widget (`enter` prints the `gh repo clone …` command; no auto-cd due to fork/execute mode).
3. **Optional zero-effort trial** — `gh extension install remcostoeten/gh-select` for a Raycast-like GitHub TUI out of the box; GitHub-only, no cd-after-clone, adds a Go binary, so it *complements* the function.

**Skip gh-dash** for this (keep for PR/issue triage). **gh-fzf** is a fine reference/drop-in if you'd rather not maintain glue, but GitHub-only and needs `enter` rebound. If sharing ever matters, factor the picker into a `gh-repo` extension and keep a 3-line shell wrapper that adds `cd` (more surface to maintain).

## 1. gh CLI capabilities
- `gh repo list [owner] --limit N` — **default 30**; use `--limit 4000` for "all". No documented cap.

- Filters: `--source` (non-forks), `--fork`, `--archived`, `--no-archived`, `--visibility {public|private|internal}`, `--language`, `--topic`; formatting via `--jq` / `--template`.

- `gh search repos &lt;query&gt;` searches **all of GitHub** (`--owner`, `--limit` ≤1000, `--json`) — only relevant for repos you don't own / global topic search; for "my repos" `gh repo list` is the right primitive.

```bash
  --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // "")] | @tsv'
```

```text
108	    printf '%s\n' "$usage" >&2
109	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
110	    return 1
111	  fi
112	
113	  if [ -e "$leaf" ]; then
114	    printf '%s\n' "Destination already exists: $PWD/$leaf" >&2
115	    return 1
116	  fi
117	
118	  # Count path components (subdir depth) for `tar --strip-components=N`.
119	  local strip="${#subdir_parts[@]}"
120	
121	  local archive_root="${repo}-${branch}"
122	  local tmpdir
123	  tmpdir="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ghget.XXXXXX")" || {
124	    printf '%s\n' "Failed to create temporary directory" >&2
125	    return 1
126	  }
127	
128	  printf '%s\n' "Downloading $owner/$repo/$subdir_path (branch: $branch) ..."
129	  if ! command curl -fsSL "https://github.com/$owner/$repo/archive/refs/heads/$branch.tar.gz" \
130	    | command tar -xz -C "$tmpdir" --strip-components="$strip" -f - "$archive_root/$subdir_path"; then
131	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
132	    printf '%s\n' "Failed to download or extract '$subdir_path' from '$owner/$repo' on branch '$branch'" >&2
133	    printf '%s\n' "$branch_note" >&2
134	    return 1
135	  fi
136	
137	  if [ ! -d "$tmpdir/$leaf" ]; then
138	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
139	    printf '%s\n' "Expected extracted directory was not found: $leaf" >&2
140	    return 1
141	  fi
142	
143	  if ! command mv -- "$tmpdir/$leaf" .; then
144	    command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
145	    printf '%s\n' "Failed to move extracted directory into: $PWD" >&2
146	    return 1
147	  fi
148	
149	  command rm -rf -- "$tmpdir"
150	}
```

```text
1	# 42_gitlab.sh - GitLab helpers using glab CLI (shared bash + zsh).
2	# Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/42_gitlab.zsh; the only zsh-ism was
3	# `emulate -L zsh` (gated below).
4	
5	# ==============================================================================
6	# Method 1: Direct shell function (no AI agent needed)
7	# ==============================================================================
8	
9	# Create a GitLab repo under a group from the current git repo, set origin, and push.
10	# Detects current folder name as repo name and current branch automatically.
11	#
12	# Usage:
13	#   glcreate <group> [description]
14	#
15	# Examples:
16	#   glcreate david_quick_tries
17	#   glcreate david_quick_tries "My awesome project"
18	#
19	# If no description is given, the repo is created without one.
20	# The repo is created as private by default.
21	glcreate() {
22	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
23	
24	  local group="${1:?Usage: glcreate <group> [description]}"
25	  local desc="${2:-}"
26	  local name
27	  name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
28	  local branch
29	  branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
30	
31	  echo "Creating: ${group}/${name} (branch: ${branch})"
32	
33	  glab repo create "${group}/${name}" \
34	    --private \
35	    --defaultBranch "$branch" \
36	    --skipGitInit \
37	    ${desc:+--description "$desc"} \
38	  && {
39	    # Add or update origin remote
40	    git remote add origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git" 2>/dev/null \
41	      || git remote set-url origin "git@gitlab.com:${group}/${name}.git"
42	  } \
43	  && git push -u origin "$branch"
44	}
45	
46	# ==============================================================================
47	# Method 2: AI agent assisted (summarizes description from project content)
48	# ==============================================================================
49	
50	# Create a GitLab repo using an AI coding agent to inspect the project,
51	# auto-generate a description, create the repo, set origin, and push.
52	#
53	# Supported agents: opencode (default), claude, codex, cursor-agent
54	# Set GLCREATE_AGENT to change the default agent.
55	# Set GLCREATE_LANG to change the default prompt language (zh or en, default: zh).
56	#
57	# Usage:
58	#   glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent <name>] [--lang zh|en]
59	#
60	# Examples:
61	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries
62	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries "Override description"
63	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --agent claude
64	#   glcreate-ai david_quick_tries --lang en
65	#
66	# If no description is given, the agent will summarize one from the project content.
67	glcreate-ai() {
68	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
69	
70	  local group="" desc="" agent="${GLCREATE_AGENT:-opencode}" lang="${GLCREATE_LANG:-zh}"
71	
72	  # Parse arguments
73	  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
74	    case "$1" in
75	      --agent) agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76	      --lang)  lang="$2"; shift 2 ;;
77	      *) [ -z "$group" ] && group="$1" || desc="$1"; shift ;;
78	    esac
79	  done
80	
81	  if [ -z "$group" ]; then
82	    echo "Usage: glcreate-ai <group> [description] [--agent opencode|claude|codex|cursor-agent] [--lang zh|en]"
83	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_AGENT env var to change default agent (default: opencode)"
84	    echo "  Set GLCREATE_LANG  env var to change default language (default: zh)"
85	    return 1
86	  fi
87	
88	  local name
89	  name=$(basename "$(pwd)")
90	  local branch
91	  branch=$(git symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "main")
92	  local prompt
93	
94	  case "$lang" in
95	    en)
96	      prompt="Use glab to create a private repo under gitlab.com/${group}, repo name: ${name}, default branch: ${branch}. Set the origin remote and push.${desc:+ Description: ${desc}.} If no description is provided, summarize one sentence from the project content."
97	      ;;
98	    zh|*)
99	      prompt="用 glab 把這個 repo 建到 gitlab.com/${group} 底下，repo name: ${name}，private，default branch: ${branch}，設定 origin remote 並 push。${desc:+Description: ${desc}。}如果沒給 description 就根據項目內容總結一句。"
100	      ;;
101	  esac
102	
103	  echo "Agent: ${agent} | Lang: ${lang} | Repo: ${group}/${name} | Branch: ${branch}"
104	
105	  case "$agent" in
106	    opencode)       opencode run "$prompt" ;;
107	    claude)         claude -p "$prompt" ;;
108	    codex)          codex exec "$prompt" ;;
109	    cursor-agent)   cursor-agent -p "$prompt" ;;
110	    *)              echo "Unknown agent: ${agent}"; return 1 ;;
111	  esac
112	}
113
```
