```text
1	# GitHub CLI (`gh`) auth
2	
3	[`gh`](https://cli.github.com/) is the official GitHub CLI. This repo installs it via the `devtools` ansible role and uses it for issue/PR workflows, the `gh-dash` extension, and (most importantly for this page) **as the credential helper for `git push`/`git fetch` over HTTPS**.
4	
5	Two things on this page:
6	
7	1. How to authenticate `gh` so HTTPS git operations work without typing a token.
8	2. **How this repo's chezmoi-managed `~/.gitconfig` coexists with `gh auth setup-git`** — important if you're new to the dotfiles, because there's a non-obvious modify_ script involved.
9	
10	## Quick auth
11	
12	```bash
13	# Interactive: pick https + "Login with a web browser"
14	gh auth login
15	
16	# When asked "Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials?", answer Yes.
17	# That runs `gh auth setup-git` for you, which writes the credential helper
18	# into ~/.gitconfig (see next section).
19	```
20	
21	To verify:
22	
23	```bash
24	gh auth status                  # token scopes + which account
25	git config --get-all credential."https://github.com".helper
26	# Expected:
27	#   (empty line)
28	#   !/opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth git-credential   ← path varies per machine
29	```
30	
31	To re-run just the git-credential setup without re-logging in:
32	
33	```bash
34	gh auth setup-git
35	```
36	
37	To remove:
38	
39	```bash
40	gh auth logout                  # clears token + helper
41	```
42	
43	## How `gh auth setup-git` interacts with chezmoi
44	
45	`gh auth setup-git` writes two sections into `~/.gitconfig`:
46	
47	```gitconfig
48	[credential "https://github.com"]
49		helper =
50		helper = !/opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth git-credential
51	[credential "https://gist.github.com"]
52		helper =
53		helper = !/opt/homebrew/bin/gh auth git-credential
54	```
55	
56	Two non-obvious things about that block:
57	
58	1. **The empty `helper =` line is intentional**, not a bug. It resets any inherited helper (e.g. macOS Keychain's `osxkeychain`) for `github.com` so `gh` is the only authority. Without it, the OS keychain helper would race with `gh` and you'd see "Bad credentials" errors after rotating tokens.
59	2. **The path to `gh` is absolute and machine-specific**:
60	   - Apple Silicon homebrew: `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`
61	   - Intel mac homebrew: `/usr/local/bin/gh`
62	   - Linuxbrew: `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/gh`
63	   - apt / dnf / official `.deb`: `/usr/bin/gh`
64	
65	The path is hard-coded by `gh` at the moment you run `gh auth setup-git` on that machine. There is no portable form (it intentionally bypasses `PATH` so `git` doesn't pick up a different `gh` binary later).
66	
67	### Why a plain `~/.gitconfig` template would break this
68	
69	If `~/.gitconfig` were a normal chezmoi template, every `chezmoi apply` would overwrite the entire file — including the `[credential "..."]` blocks that `gh` just wrote. The next `git push` would either:
70	
71	- Fail with no helper → re-prompt for credentials interactively, or
72	- Ping-pong: you'd run `gh auth setup-git` again, and the next `chezmoi apply` would clobber it again.
73	
74	This is exactly the "out-of-band tool rewrites a managed file" problem that chezmoi's `modify_` prefix exists to solve.
75	
76	### What this repo actually does
77	
78	`~/.gitconfig` is managed by [`modify_dot_gitconfig.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/modify_dot_gitconfig.tmpl), a `modify_`-prefixed bash script that runs on every `chezmoi apply`. The script:
79	
80	1. Reads the current `~/.gitconfig` from stdin (chezmoi's `modify_` contract).
81	2. Emits the chezmoi-managed baseline — `[user]`, `[http]`, `[filter "lfs"]`, `[init]`, `[core]`, optional `[delta]` blocks, and `[include] path = ~/.gitconfig.local`.
82	3. Re-emits any `[credential "<URL>"]` sections found in the live file **verbatim**, including the gh-injected absolute path.
83	
84	Net effect: you can run `gh auth setup-git` once per machine, and `chezmoi apply` will preserve the helper forever after — no ping-pong, no per-machine template branching, no need to commit machine-specific paths.
85	
86	The `modify_` prefix is documented at [chezmoi prefixes](chezmoi-prefixes.md). The case study for this specific file is mentioned in the same place.
87	
88	## Three places per-machine git config can live
89	
90	| Place | Managed by | When to use |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| chezmoi baseline (`modify_dot_gitconfig.tmpl`) | This repo | Settings shared across all your machines (`user.email`, `init.defaultBranch`, `core.pager = delta`, …). Edit the template and `chezmoi apply`. |
93	| `[credential "<URL>"]` in `~/.gitconfig` | `gh auth setup-git` | HTTPS auth via gh. Run `gh auth login` once per machine; chezmoi preserves it. **Don't hand-edit these blocks** — let gh own them. |
94	| `~/.gitconfig.local` | You, by hand | Per-machine overrides chezmoi can't predict: `http.proxy`, `safe.directory`, work-account email overrides, `[includeIf "gitdir:..."]` for separate identities, `[url "..."]` rewrites for a corporate mirror, etc. Loaded via `[include]` from the baseline. Git-ignored by chezmoi. |
95	
96	The three layers compose left-to-right (later wins for the same key), which mirrors the `~/.zshrc` → `~/.zshrc.local` → `~/.zshrc.adhoc` pattern used elsewhere in this repo.
97	
98	## What is NOT preserved by the modify_ script
99	
100	The awk filter inside `modify_dot_gitconfig.tmpl` matches **only** `^[credential "<URL>"]` (with a quoted URL scope). Anything else in the live `~/.gitconfig` is replaced by the baseline on the next apply. In particular:
101	
102	- A bare `[credential]` (no URL scope) is **not** preserved.
103	- `[user]`, `[core]`, `[alias]`, etc. that you hand-edited into `~/.gitconfig` are **silently overwritten**. Use `~/.gitconfig.local` for those.
104	- `[credential.helper]` style flat keys (no section header) are **not** preserved. Stick to the URL-scoped section form, which is what `gh auth setup-git` writes.
105	
106	If you need to preserve another section type (e.g. `[includeIf "gitdir:~/work/"]` written by some other tool), the awk rule is the single place to extend — see the script for the pattern.
107	
108	## Troubleshooting
109	
110	**`fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`** in CI / non-interactive shell after `chezmoi apply`:
111	
112	- Check the credential block survived: `git config --get-all credential."https://github.com".helper` should show two lines (empty + `!.../gh auth git-credential`).
113	- If the second line is missing, `gh auth setup-git` was never run on this machine. Run `gh auth login` (or `gh auth setup-git` if a token is already stored).
114	- If both lines were there but git still prompts, `gh` itself may be unauthenticated: `gh auth status` should print a green check, not "not logged in".
115	
116	**`gh auth status` prints token but `git push` still prompts**:
117	
118	- The absolute path in the helper line points to a `gh` binary that no longer exists (you migrated mac → mac via Migration Assistant, or rebuilt Linuxbrew). Re-run `gh auth setup-git` to refresh the path; chezmoi will preserve the new one.
119	
120	**`chezmoi diff ~/.gitconfig` shows churn after every `gh` operation**:
121	
122	- Expected to be empty. If it isn't, the awk filter probably doesn't recognise the section header gh wrote (older or newer `gh` versions might use a different scope URL). Open the live file and the rendered output side by side: `chezmoi cat ~/.gitconfig | diff - ~/.gitconfig`. If the diff is in a `[credential "<URL>"]` block, the script has a bug — file an issue.
123	
124	## Related

1	# 32_try.zsh - try-cli configuration (ephemeral workspace manager)
2	# https://github.com/tobi/try
3	
4	# Preserve user overrides, but default the graduate destination to the
5	# normalized parent of TRY_PATH so Ctrl-G has a predictable target.
6	# https://github.com/tobi/try/commit/4bb73376044e1ed8149a66513cec42155bb9f0d3
7	export TRY_PATH="${TRY_PATH:-$HOME/src/tries}"
8	export TRY_PATH="${TRY_PATH:A}"
9	export TRY_PROJECTS="${TRY_PROJECTS:-${TRY_PATH:h}}"
10	
11	# Cached try-cli init: avoids two ruby cold starts (~67ms) on every shell
12	# startup. Mtime check on the ruby binary auto-invalidates after a `mise
13	# install ruby@<NEW>`. After a gem-only upgrade (`gem update try-cli`),
14	# force-refresh with `try-update-completion`. The gem wrapper itself is
15	# broken due to a __FILE__ == $0 guard, hence the indirect ruby try.rb call.
16	_try_cache="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/zsh/try_init.zsh"
17	_try_ruby="$(command -v ruby 2>/dev/null)"
18	if [[ -n "$_try_ruby" ]] && { [[ ! -f "$_try_cache" ]] || [[ "$_try_ruby" -nt "$_try_cache" ]]; }; then
19	    _try_script=$(ruby -e "require 'rubygems'; puts File.join(Gem::Specification.find_by_name('try-cli').gem_dir, 'try.rb')" 2>/dev/null)
20	    if [[ -f "$_try_script" ]]; then
21	        mkdir -p "${_try_cache:h}"
22	        ruby "$_try_script" init > "$_try_cache" 2>/dev/null
23	    fi
24	    unset _try_script
25	fi
26	[[ -s "$_try_cache" ]] || { unset _try_cache _try_ruby; return 0; }
27	source "$_try_cache"
28	unset _try_cache _try_ruby
29	
30	# ── try + sesh integration ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
31	# Open a try project and immediately start a sesh coding session.
32	# Usage:
33	#   try-sesh some-project       # fuzzy-match or create, then sesh connect
34	#   try-sesh https://github.com/user/repo  # clone, then sesh connect
35	#
36	# The session name follows sesh's dir_length=2 convention:
37	#   e.g. "tries/2026-04-14-some-project"
38	function try-sesh() {
39	    if ! command -v sesh &>/dev/null; then
40	        echo "try-sesh: sesh not found" >&2
41	        return 1
42	    fi
43	    # Run try, which cd's into the project directory
44	    try "$@" || return $?
45	    # Now connect sesh to the directory try landed in
46	    sesh connect "$PWD"
47	}
48	
49	alias tsesh='try-sesh'
50

# Plan: Interactive GitHub/GitLab repo finder (`ghrepo` / `glrepo` + tv twins)

## Context

Finding one's own repos today means opening `github.com/daviddwlee84?tab=repositories`
and eyeballing name/description, or running `gh repo list` — which is **non-interactive
and caps at 30 rows** by default. The goal: fuzzy-search your repos by *name + description*,
preview the README in-terminal, then act — **clone (and `cd` in)**, **open in browser**, or
**copy the URL**. Same for GitLab. Raycast's GitHub extension is the UX target, but in the
terminal, reusing this repo's existing idioms.

**Research outcome (why this shape).** Both `gh` and `glab` are *already installed* (ansible
`devtools` role), so no new binaries are required. The decisive constraint: the workflow is
find → clone → **work in the repo**, and only code running in the interactive shell (a shell
function) can `cd` the parent shell into a freshly-cloned dir — a `gh` *extension* or a `tv`
*action* runs in a subprocess and cannot. Prebuilt options exist (`remcostoeten/gh-select`,
`benelan/gh-fzf`) but are GitHub-only and can't `cd`-after-clone. So the primary surface is a
pair of **shell functions**, with **`tv` channels as discoverable browse/open/copy twins** —
mirroring this repo's existing `mlf` ↔ `tv mlflow` twin pattern.

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **Surfaces:** shell functions **+** tv channel twins.
- **Clone destination:** default = **current dir, then `cd <repo>`**; expose a `*_ROOT` env
  hook now so a "repo root" (e.g. `~/src`) can be wired later to pair with try-cli's `graduate`
  (`Ctrl-G` → `$TRY_PROJECTS`). See Follow-ups.
- **GitLab:** gitlab.com now (self-hosted via `GITLAB_HOST` is a documented follow-up).

## What already exists (reuse — do not reinvent)

| Thing | Path | Reuse for |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub shell-fn home | `dot_config/shell/41_github.sh` (`ghget`) | add `ghrepo` here (POSIX, bash+zsh) |
| GitLab shell-fn home | `dot_config/shell/42_gitlab.sh` (`glcreate`) | add `glrepo` here |
| tv channel template | `dot_config/television/cable/git-ops.toml` | copy `_clip()` action + `{split:\t:N}` + keybinding style |
| tv channel template | `dot_config/television/cable/fleet-hosts.toml` | house style: CLI source → TSV → `display`/`output` |
| gh doc | `docs/tools/gh-cli.md` | add a "Find & clone your repos" section |
| clone-dir convention | `dot_config/sesh/sesh.toml` wildcards (`/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*`, `~/repos/*`) | Follow-up repo-root target |
| try graduate | `dot_config/zsh/tools/32_try.zsh` (`TRY_PROJECTS`, `try-sesh`) | Follow-up integration |

Community `gh-prs.toml` / `git-repos.toml` exist only in the *live* cable dir (from
`tv update-channels`), unmanaged — cribbing references, not files to edit.

## Design

Two cross-platform shell functions + two tv channels. Both hosts symmetric (GitHub via `gh`,
GitLab via `glab`). The fzf/tv key mnemonics are aligned where the platform allows: **`ctrl-y`
= copy-URL** and **`alt-o` = open-in-browser** in both surfaces; clone is `enter` in the
functions (can `cd`) vs `alt-c` in the channels (subprocess, can't `cd`) — that divergence *is*
the cd-constraint story and gets a one-line doc note.

### 1. `ghrepo` — append to `dot_config/shell/41_github.sh`

POSIX/shared style matching `ghget` (`command -v` guards, `local`, no zsh-only constructs).
`cd` works in-place because a function does not spawn a subshell.

\```sh
# Fuzzy-find your GitHub repos (name + description), preview README, then
# clone+cd / open in browser / copy URL. Needs: gh (authed) + fzf.
# Usage: ghrepo [owner] [extra `gh repo list` flags]
#   ghrepo                  # your repos (default owner = authed user)
#   ghrepo some-org --source
# Clone lands in ${GHREPO_ROOT:-$PWD}/<repo>, then cd's in.
ghrepo() {
  command -v gh  >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ghrepo: gh not found"  >&2; return 1; }
  command -v fzf >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ghrepo: fzf not found" >&2; return 1; }
  local sel repo dest
  sel=$(
    gh repo list "$@" --limit 4000 --no-archived \
       --json nameWithOwner,description,primaryLanguage,visibility \
       --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // ""), (.primaryLanguage.name // ""), .visibility] | @tsv' \
    | fzf --ansi --delimiter='\t' --with-nth=1,2,3,4 \
          --preview 'gh repo view {1}' --preview-window='right,60%,wrap' \
          --header 'enter=clone+cd  alt-o=open  ctrl-y=copy-url' \
          --bind 'alt-o:execute-silent(gh repo view {1} --web)' \
          --bind 'ctrl-y:execute-silent(gh browse -R {1} -n | (pbcopy 2>/dev/null || wl-copy 2>/dev/null || xclip -selection clipboard 2>/dev/null))' \
    | cut -f1
  )
  [ -n "$sel" ] || return 0
  repo="${sel##*/}"; dest="${GHREPO_ROOT:-$PWD}"
  gh repo clone "$sel" "$dest/$repo" && cd "$dest/$repo"
}
\```
Key points: `--limit 4000` (lists *all* repos, not 30); private repos included when authed;
name+description both fuzzy-searchable; `gh repo view {1}` renders the README as the preview.

### 2. `glrepo` — append to `dot_config/shell/42_gitlab.sh`

Mirror of `ghrepo` using `glab`. `web_url` is carried as a hidden TSV field for copy (glab has
no `browse -n`). gitlab.com by default; `glab` honors `GITLAB_HOST` natively for self-hosted.

\```sh
# Fuzzy-find your GitLab repos, preview, clone+cd / open / copy URL.
# Needs: glab (authed) + fzf + jq. Usage: glrepo [extra `glab repo list` flags]
glrepo() {
  command -v glab >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "glrepo: glab not found" >&2; return 1; }
  command -v fzf  >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "glrepo: fzf not found"  >&2; return 1; }
  local sel repo dest
  sel=$(
    glab repo list --mine --per-page 100 "$@" -F json \
    | jq -r '.[] | [.path_with_namespace, (.description // ""), .visibility, .web_url] | @tsv' \
    | fzf --ansi --delimiter='\t' --with-nth=1,2,3 \
          --preview 'glab repo view {1}' --preview-window='right,60%,wrap' \
          --header 'enter=clone+cd  alt-o=open  ctrl-y=copy-url' \
          --bind 'alt-o:execute-silent(glab repo view {1} --web)' \
          --bind 'ctrl-y:execute-silent(printf %s {4} | (pbcopy 2>/dev/null || wl-copy 2>/dev/null || xclip -selection clipboard 2>/dev/null))' \
    | cut -f1
  )
  [ -n "$sel" ] || return 0
  repo="${sel##*/}"; dest="${GLREPO_ROOT:-$PWD}"
  glab repo clone "$sel" "$dest/$repo" && cd "$dest/$repo"
}
\```
Note: `--per-page 100`; add `--all` in-line comment for users with >100 repos.

### 3. `dot_config/television/cable/github-repos.toml` (new, plain `.toml`)

`requirements = ["gh", "jq"]` auto-skips the channel where the binaries are absent (cleaner
than a `.tmpl` OS gate). `enter` stays tv's default `confirm_selection` (emits `nameWithOwner`
via `output`, so `sel=$(tv github-repos)` works); side-effects on Alt/Ctrl. `_clip()` body and
the `{split:\\t:N}` escaping are copied verbatim from `git-ops.toml`.

\```toml
[metadata]
name = "github-repos"
description = "Fuzzy-find your GitHub repos: preview README, open, copy URL, clone"
requirements = ["gh", "jq"]

[source]
command = "gh repo list --limit 4000 --no-archived --json nameWithOwner,description,primaryLanguage,visibility --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // \"\"), (.primaryLanguage.name // \"\"), .visibility] | @tsv'"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:3}  {split:\\t:2}  │  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[ui]
layout = "portrait"
[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[preview]
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
alt-o = "actions:open"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-url"
alt-c = "actions:clone"

[actions.open]
description = "Open repo in browser"
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}' --web"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy-url]
description = "Copy repo URL to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; gh browse -R '{split:\\t:0}' -n | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clone]
description = "Clone repo into the current directory"
command = """repo='{split:\\t:0}'; printf '\\nCloning %s ...\\n' "$repo"; gh repo clone "$repo"; printf '\\n[Press Enter to close]'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"
\```

### 4. `dot_config/television/cable/gitlab-repos.toml` (new)

Same shape with `glab`, `requirements = ["glab", "jq"]`, source
`glab repo list --mine --per-page 100 -F json | jq -r '.[] | [.path_with_namespace, (.description // ""), .visibility, .web_url] | @tsv'`.
`copy-url` action pipes `printf '%s' '{split:\\t:3}'` (the `web_url`) into `_clip()`;
`open`/`clone` use `glab repo view --web` / `glab repo clone`.

`requirements = ["gh", "jq"]` auto-skips the channel where the binaries are absent (cleaner
than a `.tmpl` OS gate). `enter` stays tv's default `confirm_selection` (emits `nameWithOwner`
via `output`, so `sel=$(tv github-repos)` works); side-effects on Alt/Ctrl. `_clip()` body and
the `{split:\\t:N}` escaping are copied verbatim from `git-ops.toml`.

```toml
[metadata]
name = "github-repos"
description = "Fuzzy-find your GitHub repos: preview README, open, copy URL, clone"
requirements = ["gh", "jq"]

[source]
command = "gh repo list --limit 4000 --no-archived --json nameWithOwner,description,primaryLanguage,visibility --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // \"\"), (.primaryLanguage.name // \"\"), .visibility] | @tsv'"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:3}  {split:\\t:2}  │  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[ui]
layout = "portrait"
[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[preview]
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}'"

[keybindings]
alt-o = "actions:open"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-url"
alt-c = "actions:clone"

[actions.open]
description = "Open repo in browser"
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}' --web"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy-url]
description = "Copy repo URL to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; gh browse -R '{split:\\t:0}' -n | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clone]
description = "Clone repo into the current directory"
command = """repo='{split:\\t:0}'; printf '\\nCloning %s ...\\n' "$repo"; gh repo clone "$repo"; printf '\\n[Press Enter to close]'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"
```

### 4. `dot_config/television/cable/gitlab-repos.toml` (new)

Same shape with `glab`, `requirements = ["glab", "jq"]`, source
`glab repo list --mine --per-page 100 -F json | jq -r '.[] | [.path_with_namespace, (.description // ""), .visibility, .web_url] | @tsv'`.
`copy-url` action pipes `printf '%s' '{split:\\t:3}'` (the `web_url`) into `_clip()`;
`open`/`clone` use `glab repo view --web` / `glab repo clone`.

## Mandatory cross-file updates (same commit — per CLAUDE.md)

- **`docs/shells/aliases.md`** — add rows for `ghrepo` and `glrepo` next to `ghget`/`glcreate`
  (columns: name | type=function | source file | scope | one-line). *(Hard rule: shell fn in
  `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` → aliases.md row.)*
- **`docs/tools/tv.md`** — add `github-repos` / `gitlab-repos` to the channel reference list.
- **`docs/tools/gh-cli.md`** — add a short "Finding & cloning your repos" section (`ghrepo`
  + `tv github-repos`, the `--limit 4000` vs default-30 note, the cd-constraint one-liner).
- If any edited doc has a `.zh-TW.md` twin, mirror the change; then `uv run mkdocs build --strict`
  (aware of the ~12 baseline warnings tracked in memory — not a regression from this change).

**Not required:** no completion files (these are shell *functions*, not `dot_dotfiles/bin`
CLIs, so the Section-F two-file rule doesn't apply); **no** `chezmoi-dotfiles` SKILL.md edit
(tv channels are auto-discovered; the skill is only edited for a new prompt key or a stable new
`executable_*` CLI); no `mkdocs.yml` nav change (extending existing docs, not adding pages);
no ansible/tool-managers change (`gh`/`glab` already installed).

## Verification (run the app, not just syntax — per Hard invariant)

1. `chezmoi diff` then `chezmoi apply`.
2. `gh auth status` (prereq). Reload: `exec zsh` (or `source ~/.config/shell/41_github.sh`).

6. Edge cases: ESC in fzf returns cleanly (no clone); a repo whose name != dir basename clones

# GitHub repos cable channel for television (tv) — browse twin of the `ghrepo`
# shell function (dot_config/shell/41_github.sh).
#
# Fuzzy-find your GitHub repos, preview the README, then open in browser, copy
# the URL, or clone. Needs gh (authenticated) + jq; auto-skipped where either is
# absent (see `requirements`).
#
# Usage:
#   tv github-repos                 (Enter prints owner/repo; Alt+O opens; Ctrl+Y copies URL; Alt+C clones)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Print owner/repo to stdout (TV default confirm_selection; for `sel=$(tv github-repos)`)
#   Alt+O      Open the repo on github.com               (fork — TUI stays open)
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy the repo URL to clipboard            (overrides TV's full-line copy)
#   Alt+C      Clone into tv's launch cwd                (execute — shows progress)
#
# NB: a tv action runs in a subprocess and cannot cd your shell after cloning —
# use the `ghrepo` function for the clone+cd flow. `--limit 4000` lists *all*
# repos (plain `gh repo list` stops at 30).
#
# Source format (TSV columns):
#   0. nameWithOwner   (raw; printed / previewed / cloned / opened)
#   1. description
#   2. primaryLanguage
#   3. visibility

[metadata]
name = "github-repos"
description = "Fuzzy-find your GitHub repos: preview README, open, copy URL, clone"
requirements = ["gh", "jq"]

[source]
command = "gh repo list --limit 4000 --no-archived --json nameWithOwner,description,primaryLanguage,visibility --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // \"\"), (.primaryLanguage.name // \"\"), .visibility] | @tsv'"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:3}  {split:\\t:2}  │  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[ui]
layout = "portrait"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[preview]
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}'"
header = "{split:\\t:0}"

[keybindings]
# Alt+ for side effects (Ctrl+letter is shadowed by tmux root table); Ctrl+Y
# overrides TV's default full-line copy to copy just the repo URL.
alt-o = "actions:open"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-url"
alt-c = "actions:clone"

[actions.open]
description = "Open repo in browser"
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}' --web"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy-url]
description = "Copy repo URL to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; gh browse -R '{split:\\t:0}' -n | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clone]
description = "Clone repo into the current directory"
command = """repo='{split:\\t:0}'; printf '\\nCloning %s ...\\n' "$repo"; gh repo clone "$repo"; printf '\\n[Press Enter to close]'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[source]
command = "glab repo list --mine --per-page 100 -F json | jq -r '.[] | [.path_with_namespace, (.description // \"\"), .visibility, .web_url] | @tsv'"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:2}  │  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[ui]
layout = "portrait"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[preview]
command = "glab repo view '{split:\\t:0}'"
header = "{split:\\t:0}"

[keybindings]
alt-o = "actions:open"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-url"
alt-c = "actions:clone"

[actions.open]
description = "Open project in browser"
command = "glab repo view '{split:\\t:0}' --web"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy-url]
description = "Copy project URL to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:3}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clone]
description = "Clone project into the current directory"
command = """repo='{split:\\t:0}'; printf '\\nCloning %s ...\\n' "$repo"; glab repo clone "$repo"; printf '\\n[Press Enter to close]'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

The channel uses `watch = 2.0`, so rows stream into the picker as the background scan progresses (state column: `discovered` → `scanning` → `scanned`).

133:3. **Linux only** — `journalctl --output=short-iso -n 2000` for systemd journal recent lines. Templated out on macOS because journalctl output lines are not file paths and the preview/Enter/Alt+T actions can't act on them (a dedicated `tv journalctl` channel would be the follow-up).

200:**Why this exists vs the generic `kill-process` channel**: `kill-process` sorts by RSS via `ps -axm`. On Apple Silicon, RSS does NOT include compressed or swapped pages — a process leaking 2 GB of compressed data shows as 100 MB in the RSS view. `mac-procs` uses `top -o mem` whose `mem` column is compressed-aware. See [macos-swap.md](macos-swap.md) for the full mental model.

The filtered view has preview but not the full action keybindings. Quit to return to the main `tv pueue` channel. Enter on the groups source (cycle 4) shows a quick text overview via `pueue status -g`.
351:- `Ctrl+Y` is overridden in the pueue channel to copy just the raw command (TV's default `ctrl-y` copies the full display line including ID, status, and group)
356:### `azure` channel
358:Fuzzy-search Azure resources via `az` CLI with per-resource actions: restart / start / power-off / deallocate / rotate-public-IP / SSH / open-in-portal / delete / copy-id / switch-subscription. Backed by three helper scripts under `~/.config/television/` (`azure-source.sh`, `azure-preview.sh`, `azure-rotate-ip.sh`). Requires `az` (ansible `iac_tools` tag) and `jq`; the channel is automatically skipped on hosts without either.
362:**Login gate:** if `az account show` fails, the channel shows a single synthetic row (`login · not-logged-in`). Press `Enter` to run `az login`, then `Ctrl+R` to reload.

258	
259	Each row also shows the matching **oh-my-zsh `git` plugin alias** (`gc!`, `gcam`, `gpf!`, `gst`, `grhh`, `gstp`, …) or repo-custom function (prefixed `*`, e.g. `*gcam-amend`, `*gundo`, `*lg`). That means you can fuzzy-search either by semantic name (`amend`, `undo`, `force push`), by the full `git …` invocation, **or** by the alias you half-remember — any of them lands on the same row.
260	
261	Open with `tv git-ops` (standalone) or press `Alt+I` in zsh to paste the selected command straight into the shell prompt.
262	
263	| Key | Action |
264	|-----|--------|
265	| `Enter` | Print selected command to stdout — captured by the `Alt+I` ZLE widget and inserted into `LBUFFER` |
266	| `Ctrl+Y` | Copy command to clipboard (overrides TV default; pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / OSC 52 fallback) |
267	| `Alt+E` | Confirm-prompt then `eval` the command (y/N); aborts by default on anything else |
268	| `Ctrl+F` | Cycle preview: matching row from `git-ops.md` ↔ `git help <subcommand>` |
269	| `Ctrl+O` | Toggle preview panel (TV global) |
270	
271	> `Alt+E` (not `Ctrl+E`) is used for execute so that TV's global `Ctrl+E = go_to_input_end` muscle memory is preserved inside the picker.
272	
273	Destructive rows (`commit --amend`, `reset --hard`, `push --force`, `branch -D`, `clean -fd`, `stash drop/clear`, `tag -d` on remote, rebase, etc.) are prefixed with `⚠` in the display line and trigger a red warning banner under `Alt+E`.
274	
275	Use-cases this solves:
276	
277	- "What's the exact `git commit --amend --no-edit` flag again?" — type `amend` or `gcn!`, Enter, done.
278	- "How do I undo the last commit without losing work?" — type `undo` or `gundo`, you see all three variants (soft / mixed / hard with the destructive tag).
279	- "Which alias force-pushes safely?" — type `force`, see `gpf` (with-lease, safe) next to `gpf!` (raw `--force`, destructive).
280	- Copy a command into a Cursor chat or a teammate's Slack without typing — `Ctrl+Y`.
281	- `git worktree`, `git submodule`, `git cherry-pick` — the commands nobody remembers the flags for.

3	## Ansible on macOS
4	- `ansible.builtin.unarchive` with `.tar.gz` fails on macOS because it requires GNU tar, but macOS ships BSD tar. Use `.zip` assets instead (macOS has `/usr/bin/unzip` built-in).
5	- The ansible runner script (`run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl`) only passes `BECOME_FLAGS` (sudo) on Linux, not macOS. Any `become: true` task will fail on macOS with "sudo: a password is required". Put macOS sudo operations in shell scripts instead.

13	- `run_once_before_*` — runs once ever (bootstrap)

```sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Repo-list source for the `ghrepo` picker (dot_config/shell/41_github.sh) and
# the `github-repos` tv channel. Emits TSV:
#   nameWithOwner \t description \t primaryLanguage \t visibility
#
# Stale-while-revalidate cache at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tv/gh-repos.tsv:
#   * prints the cached list immediately — the picker opens instantly after the
#     first run instead of waiting on the GitHub API (~300+ repos = a few sec)
#   * if the cache is older than GHREPO_CACHE_TTL seconds (default 3600), a
#     detached background fetch refreshes it for the NEXT launch
#   * first run (no cache yet) fetches synchronously
#   * `--refresh` forces a synchronous refetch (the picker's Ctrl-R / Alt-R)
#
# Keep the TSV columns in sync with both consumers' `cut -f` / `{split:\t:N}`.
set -uo pipefail

cache_dir="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/tv"
cache="$cache_dir/gh-repos.tsv"
ttl="${GHREPO_CACHE_TTL:-3600}"
mkdir -p "$cache_dir"

_fetch() {
  command gh repo list --limit 4000 --no-archived \
    --json nameWithOwner,description,primaryLanguage,visibility \
    --jq '.[] | [.nameWithOwner, (.description // ""), (.primaryLanguage.name // ""), .visibility] | @tsv'
}

_refresh_now() {
  local tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp "${cache}.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  if _fetch >"$tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$tmp" ]; then
    mv -f "$tmp" "$cache"
  else
    rm -f "$tmp"
    return 1
  fi
}

# Synchronous (re)fetch when forced or when there is no cache yet.
if [ "${1:-}" = "--refresh" ] || [ ! -s "$cache" ]; then
  _refresh_now || true
fi

# Serve whatever we have.
[ -s "$cache" ] && cat "$cache"

# Background revalidate if stale (skip right after a forced refresh).
if [ "${1:-}" != "--refresh" ] && [ -s "$cache" ]; then
  now="$(date +%s)"
  mtime="$(stat -f %m "$cache" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$cache" 2>/dev/null || echo "$now")"
  if [ "$((now - mtime))" -gt "$ttl" ]; then
    # Detach fds off the picker's source pipe so fzf/tv gets EOF immediately.
    ( _refresh_now ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  fi
fi
exit 0

```

#   path_with_namespace \t description \t visibility \t web_url
#
# Stale-while-revalidate cache at $XDG_CACHE_HOME/tv/gl-repos.tsv — same model as
# gh-repos-source.sh (instant after first run; background revalidate when older
# than GLREPO_CACHE_TTL seconds, default 3600; `--refresh` forces a refetch).
# gitlab.com by default; export GITLAB_HOST for a self-hosted instance (glab
# honors it).
#
# Keep the TSV columns in sync with both consumers' `cut -f` / `{split:\t:N}`.
set -uo pipefail

cache_dir="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/tv"
cache="$cache_dir/gl-repos.tsv"
ttl="${GLREPO_CACHE_TTL:-3600}"
mkdir -p "$cache_dir"

_fetch() {
  command glab repo list --mine --per-page 100 -F json \
    | command jq -r '.[] | [.path_with_namespace, (.description // ""), .visibility, .web_url] | @tsv'
}

_refresh_now() {
  local tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp "${cache}.XXXXXX")" || return 1
  if _fetch >"$tmp" 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$tmp" ]; then
    mv -f "$tmp" "$cache"
  else
    rm -f "$tmp"
    return 1
  fi
}

if [ "${1:-}" = "--refresh" ] || [ ! -s "$cache" ]; then
  _refresh_now || true
fi

[ -s "$cache" ] && cat "$cache"

if [ "${1:-}" != "--refresh" ] && [ -s "$cache" ]; then
  now="$(date +%s)"
  mtime="$(stat -f %m "$cache" 2>/dev/null || stat -c %Y "$cache" 2>/dev/null || echo "$now")"
  if [ "$((now - mtime))" -gt "$ttl" ]; then
    ( _refresh_now ) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
  fi
fi
exit 0

```

```toml
# GitHub repos cable channel for television (tv) — browse twin of the `ghrepo`
# shell function (dot_config/shell/41_github.sh).
#
# Fuzzy-find your GitHub repos, preview the README, then open in browser, copy
# the URL, or clone. Needs gh (authenticated); auto-skipped where gh is absent.
#
# The repo list is cached (stale-while-revalidate) by the shared source helper
# ~/.config/television/gh-repos-source.sh, so the picker opens instantly after
# the first run. Ctrl+R re-reads (TV global reload_source); Alt+R forces a live
# refresh from the API.
#
# Usage:
#   tv github-repos                 (Enter prints owner/repo; Alt+O opens; Ctrl+Y copies URL; Alt+C clones)
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Print owner/repo to stdout (TV default confirm_selection; for `sel=$(tv github-repos)`)
#   Alt+O      Open the repo on github.com               (fork — TUI stays open)
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy the repo URL to clipboard            (overrides TV's full-line copy)
#   Alt+C      Clone into tv's launch cwd                (execute — shows progress)
#   Ctrl+R     Reload from cache                         (TV global reload_source)
#   Alt+R      Force a live refresh from the API, then reload
#
# NB: a tv action runs in a subprocess and cannot cd your shell after cloning —
# use the `ghrepo` function for the clone+cd flow.
#
# Source format (TSV columns):
#   0. nameWithOwner   (raw; printed / previewed / cloned / opened)
#   1. description
#   2. primaryLanguage
#   3. visibility

[metadata]
name = "github-repos"
description = "Fuzzy-find your GitHub repos: preview README, open, copy URL, clone"
requirements = ["gh"]

[source]
command = "~/.config/television/gh-repos-source.sh"
display = "{split:\\t:0}  {split:\\t:3}  {split:\\t:2}  │  {split:\\t:1}"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"

[ui]
layout = "portrait"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[preview]
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}'"
header = "{split:\\t:0}"

[keybindings]
# Alt+ for side effects (Ctrl+letter is shadowed by tmux root table); Ctrl+Y
# overrides TV's default full-line copy to copy just the repo URL.
alt-o = "actions:open"
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-url"
alt-c = "actions:clone"
alt-r = ["actions:refresh", "reload_source"]

[actions.open]
description = "Open repo in browser"
command = "gh repo view '{split:\\t:0}' --web"
mode = "fork"

[actions.copy-url]
description = "Copy repo URL to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; gh browse -R '{split:\\t:0}' -n | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.clone]
description = "Clone repo into the current directory"
command = """repo='{split:\\t:0}'; printf '\\nCloning %s ...\\n' "$repo"; gh repo clone "$repo"; printf '\\n[Press Enter to close]'; read -r _"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.refresh]
description = "Force a live refresh of the repo list (bypass cache)"
command = "printf 'Refreshing GitHub repos ...\\n'; ~/.config/television/gh-repos-source.sh --refresh >/dev/null 2>&1"
mode = "execute"

```

## 2. Caching — yes, and it was badly needed
The slowness was real: **`gh repo list` for your 326 repos takes ~15s**. Added a shared stale-while-revalidate cache (`~/.config/television/g{h,l}-repos-source.sh` → `~/.cache/tv/`):

- **Cold 15.4s → warm 0.07s** (GitHub); 5.3s → 0.07s (GitLab) — measured.
- After the first fetch, every launch is instant and revalidates in the **background** when older than 1h (`GHREPO_CACHE_TTL`).
- **`Ctrl-R`** in `ghrepo`/`glrepo` (or **`Alt-R`** in the tv channels) forces a live refresh. Passing args (`ghrepo some-org`) still queries live.

Both the functions and the tv channels share the one cache script.
